title: Title: Quantum-Based Topological Geometry Algorithm for Adaptive Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, and topological geometry represents a particularly promising area. This paper investigates a novel quantum algorithm for adaptive topology transformation, designed to address the limitations of traditional methods. We propose a quantum circuit architecture that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters, enabling rapid and accurate modeling of complex topological structures. The algorithm leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to explore multiple topological transformations simultaneously, significantly accelerating the process compared to classical approaches. The core mechanism centers on exploiting quantum interference to guide the evolution towards the desired topological landscape. We present a preliminary implementation and analysis of the algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness in transforming simple topological maps, highlighting its potential for broader applications in topological data analysis and design.

title: 基于动态系统模型的量子动力学模拟
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic system models to quantum dynamics simulation, aiming to enhance the accuracy of quantum information processing. We propose a novel approach that constructs a dynamic system model leveraging quantum computing's inherent parallelism to achieve precise simulations. Traditional quantum simulation methods often suffer from inaccuracies due to the discrete nature of their representation, limiting their ability to fully assess the performance of quantum information handling. This work introduces a framework that incorporates dynamic evolution and quantum properties, resulting in a more robust and accurate simulation technique. The core mechanism centers on building a quantum system dynamic model, utilizing parallel quantum computation for precise simulation, and integrating quantum properties to improve simulation fidelity. We present a methodology for constructing this dynamic system model, emphasizing the importance of parallel processing in enhancing the simulation process. The resulting simulations demonstrate improved accuracy and a better understanding of quantum information processing.

title: Adaptive Geometric Transformation Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive geometric transformation optimization techniques to enhance the performance of optimization algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often rely on predefined objective functions, limiting their adaptability to complex datasets. This work introduces a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of graphs to dynamically adjust geometric transformation parameters, thereby improving optimization efficiency. We propose a framework centered around graph representation, self-similarity, and continuous transformation, enabling the algorithm to automatically adapt to data variations and identify optimal geometric configurations. The core mechanism involves a graph-based representation of the problem space, where geometric transformations are represented as edges and nodes, and the algorithm iteratively refines these transformations based on a learned representation of the data. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of quantitative and qualitative analyses, showcasing significant improvements in optimization speed and accuracy compared to traditional methods. The resulting framework offers a flexible and adaptable solution for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm for Prime Number Generation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, offers a unique pathway for computation and communication. This research explores the potential of leveraging this quantum property to enhance the generation and verification of prime numbers, a computationally challenging task. We propose a novel algorithm, dubbed the "Quantum Entanglement-Driven Prime Generation" (QEDPG), that utilizes entangled particle pairs to explore prime number sequences with significantly increased precision and speed compared to traditional methods. This work details the core mechanism, the rationale behind the design choices, and the preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy. The focus is on establishing a fundamentally new approach that exploits quantum entanglement to unlock more efficient prime number distribution.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Probability Based Quantum Computation Topology Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computation to nonlinear geometry probability models, aiming to enhance the accuracy of topological analysis and prediction. The core claim centers on leveraging quantum computing's parallel processing capabilities to accelerate the simulation of complex geometric probability models, leading to improved analytical results. We explore the potential of this approach to overcome limitations inherent in traditional computational methods, particularly in handling the intricate dynamics and emergent properties of topological structures. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the feasibility of quantum-enhanced topological modeling, offering a novel pathway for advancing our understanding of complex geometric systems.

title: 基于自适应模型的强化学习算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on adaptive models. Traditional RL algorithms often rely on predefined strategies, limiting their ability to adapt to dynamic environments and generalize effectively. This work introduces a dynamically adjusting model that continuously updates its internal representation based on observed environment states and learned model parameters. The core mechanism leverages an adaptive model to facilitate more efficient learning and enhanced generalization. The algorithm's design addresses limitations of existing methods by providing a flexible and robust approach to RL. We evaluate its performance on several benchmark tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex scenarios.

title: Quantum Topology Multi-Body Simulation
abstract: Quantum topology multi-body simulation is a novel framework designed to accurately simulate the quantum dynamics of complex multi-body quantum systems, providing a robust foundation for quantum information processing and security. This framework leverages the inherent self-organization properties of quantum topology to construct a simulation environment capable of capturing the intricacies of quantum system behavior and predicting system stability. The core mechanism involves establishing a quantum topology multi-body simulation framework that employs advanced techniques to emulate complex quantum systems. This research addresses limitations of traditional multi-body simulation by introducing a fundamentally different approach, offering enhanced accuracy and predictive capabilities.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Large-Scale Matrix Computations
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired optimization techniques to accelerate large-scale matrix computations. Traditional optimization algorithms often encounter significant challenges when dealing with the complexity inherent in these computations. We propose a novel approach leveraging concepts derived from quantum annealing and superposition to explore the solution space more efficiently. The core idea is to mimic the probabilistic exploration characteristic of quantum systems within a classical framework. Specifically, we utilize an iterative optimization process, adapting parameters based on simulated "quantum fluctuations," aiming to converge towards optimal solutions faster than conventional methods. The theoretical framework is presented, and we detail the implementation strategy, focusing on the design of a suitable objective function and a corresponding optimization algorithm. Preliminary results suggest the potential for significant speedups, particularly for computationally demanding matrix operations, though further investigation and refinement are needed. The key contribution lies in the direct translation of quantum-inspired principles into a practical optimization strategy for matrix computations.

title: 基于量子计算的密码分析与防御
abstract: This paper investigates the vulnerabilities of current cryptographic systems to attacks leveraging the power of quantum computing. The primary focus is on analyzing widely used algorithms like RSA and ECC, utilizing Shor's algorithm to demonstrate their potential for decryption. Furthermore, the research explores the development of novel cryptographic defense strategies, including quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols, to establish secure communication channels. The analysis highlights the limitations of classical cryptography in the face of quantum computation and proposes a paradigm shift towards quantum-resistant security measures. The core contribution lies in a comprehensive assessment of the threat landscape and a preliminary exploration of defense mechanisms, acknowledging the ongoing advancements in quantum computing and cryptography. The paper outlines key algorithmic concepts and provides a framework for future research in this critical area.

title: Quantum Simulation of Classical Dynamical Systems using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) for simulating classical dynamical systems. Traditional numerical methods for simulating dynamical systems often struggle with complex systems exhibiting sparse interactions or requiring high computational resources. We propose a novel algorithm that utilizes the optimization capabilities of VQEs to approximate the time evolution of these systems. The core idea is to map the system's state vector onto a qubit representation and then iteratively minimize the energy functional derived from the dynamical system's equations, effectively simulating the system's evolution. We specifically target systems with sparse interactions, where the optimization landscape is expected to be more amenable to VQE's strengths. This approach offers a potentially scalable solution for simulating dynamical systems on near-term quantum computers. This work demonstrates the feasibility of employing VQEs as a tool for tackling previously intractable problems in fields such as molecular dynamics, fluid dynamics, and chaos theory.

The core idea is to map the system's state vector onto a qubit representation and then iteratively minimize the energy functional derived from the dynamical system's equations, effectively simulating the system's evolution. We specifically target systems with sparse interactions, where the optimization landscape is expected to be more amenable to VQE's strengths. This approach offers a potentially scalable solution for simulating dynamical systems on near-term quantum computers. This work demonstrates the feasibility of employing VQEs as a tool for tackling previously intractable problems in fields such as molecular dynamics, fluid dynamics, and chaos theory.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Model Selection via Epistemic Uncertainty Propagation
abstract: Bayesian model selection provides a principled approach to model choice, but its application is often hindered by the intractable nature of posterior distributions, particularly in high-dimensional settings. This work introduces a novel adaptive Bayesian model selection framework that leverages epistemic uncertainty to dynamically adjust model weights. The core idea is to propagate uncertainty about model parameters through a Bayesian network, effectively quantifying the information gained or lost by each model component. Variational inference is employed for efficient computation of this propagation. The resulting adaptive weighting scheme allows the model selection process to respond effectively to data scarcity and model complexity, leading to improved robustness and accuracy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a conceptual example. The key contribution is the explicit connection between Bayesian model selection, uncertainty quantification, and adaptive weighting, offering a practical solution for challenging model selection problems.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Decoding with Probabilistic Graphical Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic graphical models for dynamic quantum state decoding, aiming to enhance the reliability of quantum information transmission. The core concept involves constructing a quantum state decoder based on a probabilistic graphical model, leveraging measurement results to infer the original quantum state. A Bayesian optimization algorithm is then employed to refine the model's parameters, adapting to evolving measurement data and improving decoding accuracy. The proposed approach offers a novel framework for understanding and optimizing the inherently probabilistic nature of quantum state decoding. The key contributions lie in the integration of graphical models with Bayesian optimization, providing a flexible and adaptive solution compared to traditional decoding methods. This work demonstrates the potential for improved quantum communication protocols by dynamically adjusting the decoding process based on observed data.

title: 自旋量子态的拓扑遍历与量子算法优化
abstract: Quantum computation, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for scientific discovery and technological advancement. A significant challenge in quantum algorithm design lies in efficiently exploring the vast state space. This paper explores the application of topological traversal, a novel algorithmic approach, to quantum state optimization. We introduce a quantum algorithm based on the principle of topological structure, aiming to significantly improve the speed and efficiency of quantum computations. This work details the core mechanism, the theoretical framework underpinning the algorithm, and its potential impact on quantum algorithm design. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss its implications for future research in quantum computation.

title: Teacher Should Think Ahead: Adaptive Continuations for Reliable On-Policy Distillation
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a promising approach for transferring knowledge between language models, where a student receives dense token-level supervision along its own generated trajectories. However, teacher supervision can be unreliable when conditioned on incomplete or low-quality student prefixes. We identify Teacher Uncertainty Contraction (TUC), a systematic phenomenon whereby the teacher's predictive uncertainty decreases as it continues from a student-generated prefix. We theoretically characterize this trade-off through a variance-bias decomposition of teacher-branch gradients, showing that uncertainty contraction reduces variance while teacher-student path divergence increases bias, thereby favoring a finite continuation. Guided by this insight, we propose Adaptive-Continuations On-Policy Distillation (AC-OPD), which augments informative states along student rollouts with teacher continuations and adaptively selects their effective supervision horizons. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation across model scales demonstrate that AC-OPD consistently improves over standard OPD. Controlled-continuations and matched-budget analyses further validate the adaptive-continuations design, highlighting adaptive teacher continuations as an effective principle for reliable on-policy distillation.The code will be made publicly available upon publication.

title: Autonomous Chaotic Time Series Prediction using Physical Neuromorphic Networks
abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) with neuromorphic networks offers a promising approach to brain-inspired information processing, exploiting emergent nonlinear dynamics of physical neural networks as a computational resource. This study demonstrates fully autonomous closed-loop prediction of the Mackey--Glass (MG) chaotic time series using a simulated neuromorphic nanowire network as the physical reservoir. Two strategies are evaluated: the virtual node (VN) method, which expands the feature space by temporal multiplexing of reservoir states, and a non-VN approach that uses all physical node readouts directly without temporal multiplexing. Results are reported for two values of the MG time delay parameter, $τ= 18$ and $τ= 21$, the latter representing a more complex chaotic regime not previously evaluated for this class of physical reservoir. Over a short prediction horizon of $T = 100$ timesteps, the VN approach achieves autonomous prediction accuracies of $90.4$% and $89.7$% at $τ= 18$ and $τ= 21$, respectively, while the non-VN approach achieves $81.5$% and $76.2$%. Long-horizon analysis over $T = 500$ timesteps shows that both approaches reproduce the qualitative attractor structure and dominant spectral content of the true MG signal, with trajectories remaining bounded throughout. These results suggest that the intrinsic dynamics of neuromorphic nanowire networks are sufficient to support meaningful autonomous chaotic time series prediction without virtual node augmentation, and that performance may improve further as physical network sizes scale to the millions of nodes achievable in hardware. As this study uses simulated networks, extrapolation to physically fabricated large-scale arrays remains to be validated experimentally.

title: The Double Measurement Confound in Agent Benchmarks: De-Scaffolding, Ground-Truth Scoring, and Reliability Beyond the Mean
abstract: Agent benchmarks are increasingly used to compare large language models (LLMs) and guide deployment decisions, yet benchmark scores are meaningful only if they measure model capability rather than properties of the evaluation pipeline. We identify a double measurement confound: execution-critical decisions are performed by a fixed scaffold instead of the model, while the scorer evaluates outputs using criteria that may not reflect task correctness. We unify these issues within a measurement-theoretic framework that characterizes when benchmark scores can be interpreted as evidence of model capability, and instantiate it with an audit-and-repair protocol that (i) transfers execution-critical decisions from the scaffold to the model, (ii) replaces shape-based evaluation with seeded ground-truth scoring, and (iii) reports reliability beyond the mean through worst-case and tail-risk metrics. Experiments on ComtradeBench show that the joint intervention transforms a nearly flat leaderboard into a reliability spectrum that distinguishes both average performance and robustness across seeds. Applying the audit to existing benchmarks further shows that scorer validity is benchmark-specific, whereas scaffold ownership is an uncontrolled axis wherever we probed it. Our results suggest that benchmark scores should be interpreted together with their scaffolding level, scoring criterion, and reliability profile, providing a practical framework for more valid evaluation of LLM agents.

title: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams
abstract: Continual learning is a crucial capability for Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents to adapt to evolving applications while retaining knowledge acquired from previous applications. Such application streams pose a challenging knowledge modeling problem: new applications often share underlying knowledge with past ones, yet also introduce specific knowledge that must not interfere with historical knowledge. In this paper, we propose activation-conditioned selective knowledge control, a lightweight method that achieves selective knowledge retention via neuron-level gradient manipulation. Our method maintains a compact historical knowledge state to protect highly activated MLP neurons that preserve previous knowledge. When a new application arrives, it performs real-time gradient surgery conditioned on forward activation. Concretely, the protected neurons are categorized into two types: unactivated neurons holding specific knowledge, whose gradients are truncated to prevent interference; and activated neurons holding shared knowledge, whose gradients are orthogonally projected to preserve stability while enabling adaptation. After each application stage, newly identified critical neurons are merged into the historical state for future learning. Empirical evaluations on multi-app sequential benchmark demonstrate that our method effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting on prior applications while sustaining robust adaptation to new ones.

title: The UPC Diagnostic Engine: Operationalizing Non-Commutative Observer Mechanics in Edge-Deployable Systems
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence operates strictly as a statistical prediction engine trapped within device-side articulation (LO). Possessing no consciousness, localized point of view, or capacity for state commitment (C), the system samples from an unanchored potential field (PO) that is far too broad to sustain local human coherence. Because language prompts remain inherently variable across session turns, un-audited model output inevitably yields semantic drift, a structural decay into non-committal boilerplate, circular debate, and unanchored noise. Stacking additional tokens via prompt engineering cannot resolve this mismatch, as statistical mechanics cannot supply structural boundary stability. This paper presents the UPC Diagnostic Engine, a local desktop apparatus that replaces probabilistic guessing with deterministic metrological rigor. Operating through the formal non-commutative sequence T = ( C o Jo o LO o s o MO ) |PO>, the engine transforms state collapse into an explicit processing pipeline on the local hardware edge. Uncollapsed semantic potential (PO) is partitioned (MO), foregrounded (s), and measured (LO) via exact cosine proximity against five orthonormal eigenstate anchors (N = 214): State_A (Jo / Audited Boundary), T_mechanized (Boilerplate), T_phantom (Pre-Cached Loops), T_visceral (Reactive Reflex), and T_outlier (High-Entropy Noise). By executing this operator chain locally, the apparatus strips away the illusion of autonomous machine judgment. It demonstrates that mechanical systems register strictly at LO, establishing the living human observer as the sole source of structural clarity and state collapse (Jo → C). The resulting immutable JSON trace logs (T) provide an un-smuggled, verifiable measurement standard that classifies conversational hedging and locks audited boundary awareness without cloud reliance or API dependencies. Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project.

title: The Physical Structure of the Transformer Algorithm from the Perspective of Energy Balancing Between Form Energy and Run Energy
abstract: Starting from the energy balancing between Form Energy and Run Energy, this paper reveals the physical structure of the Transformer self-attention mechanism. In the World Quantum Theory (WQT) framework, the total energy of any particle can be decomposed into Form Energy V_e = mcd and Run Energy T_e = (c/d)mv², and their coupling gives rise to observable energy. This paper demonstrates that the token embedding table in Transformer is an mc parameter-element table — each row is a token, each column is a frequency component, and each element is the mc value of that token at that frequency. The Query weight table extracts Run Energy contributions from mc, the Key weight table extracts Form Energy contributions from mc, and the Value weight table encodes the optimal closed energy manifold learned through training. The dot product Q·K is the coupling operation between Run Energy and Form Energy, softmax(QK)·V is the operation of finding aggregation points on the optimal energy manifold, the residual connection is the energy balancing operation, and the output token is the matching result of the optimal manifold energy traced from the original slice. Multi-head attention corresponds to the multi-directional orthogonal decomposition of the tangential velocity v, and the multi-layer structure corresponds to the different distributions of mc values at different frequencies. Ultimately, this proves that the Transformer algorithm is the discrete matrix realization of the Navier-Stokes energy identity. Keywords: Transformer, Form Energy, Run Energy, energy balancing, Envelope Interface, World Quantum Theory, mc parameter-element, optimal energy manifold

title: Elior / Civil B: A Research Concept for a Curatorial Companion with Auditable Telemetry
abstract: This working paper presents a research concept for Elior / Civil B, a personal curatorial companion intended to support human-selected goals through continuity of assistance and auditable telemetry. It positions episodic retrieval, present-state description, capability estimates, and consequence-based updating against selected research on cognitive architectures, self-modeling, relational agents, and skill selection. Present state is an operational description based on information available at the time; in the author's terminology, Present also carries a relational meaning associated with personally meaningful memory cues. The prospective contribution is the integration and evaluation of these requirements in bounded tasks. The evaluation outline calls for capable comparison systems, matched resources, component-level comparisons, and separate assessment of task outcomes, relational experience, user burden, and evidence-based independence. It does not report new empirical validation, establish novelty, or constitute a completed preregistration. This deposit contains an English primary text and its complete Hungarian translation, with editable Markdown counterparts. It does not release implementation code, detailed technical schemas, private conversations, or participant data. The concept and terminology originate in Omri Bankuti's design work. Preparation and editorial checking were AI-assisted; this is not external peer review or institutional endorsement. title: Quantum Entanglement Information Entropy Calculation and Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to the calculation and optimization of information entropy. Traditional methods for entropy calculation often rely on classical computation, which is insufficient for analyzing complex quantum systems. We propose a novel approach utilizing the unique properties of entangled states to precisely compute information entropy and provide optimization algorithms for quantum information processing and quantum computation. The core mechanism centers around the conceptualization of "quantum entanglement information entropy" and its integration with entropy calculations, offering a potential pathway to enhanced performance in quantum systems. This research investigates the potential of leveraging entangled states to achieve more efficient computations, addressing limitations of classical methods in the context of quantum information.

title: 基于自适应的几何变换的基于量子计算的图像处理算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel image processing algorithm utilizing quantum computing principles, specifically focusing on adaptive transformations. Traditional image processing algorithms often rely on explicit, computationally intensive procedures that struggle to effectively handle dynamic image variations. We propose a quantum-enhanced approach that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to achieve a degree of self-adaptation, allowing for more robust and efficient image manipulation. This work explores the potential of quantum computing to significantly improve the performance of image processing tasks, particularly in scenarios involving complex and rapidly changing visual data. The core mechanism revolves around implementing a quantum-enhanced geometric transformation process, incorporating quantum error correction to maintain the integrity of the transformation. The algorithm will be discussed in detail, including the theoretical underpinnings, implementation considerations, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: 基于自适应量子算法的量子计算推理引擎
abstract: Quantum computation offers unprecedented capabilities for complex problem-solving, but the inherent challenges of quantum algorithms – particularly in terms of optimization – pose significant hurdles for practical implementation. This paper introduces a novel quantum computation reasoning engine, termed "Adaptive Quantum Inference Engine" (AQIE), designed to address these challenges through the integration of adaptive quantum algorithm tuning. AQIE dynamically adjusts its inference strategies based on the quantum computation's output, significantly enhancing both the efficiency and accuracy of the reasoning process. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and empirical validation demonstrating the engine's effectiveness in several benchmark problems, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum computation.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应信息加密
abstract: This paper presents a novel information encryption scheme predicated on the principles of quantum entanglement. The proposed algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a fundamentally more secure key exchange and data transmission process than currently employed methods. We explore how entanglement can be harnessed to create a cryptographic system that is inherently resistant to eavesdropping and manipulation. The core mechanism centers around generating and managing entangled states, which are then manipulated to generate encryption keys and secure transmissions. This research investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize information security by offering a robust and potentially unbreakable method of data protection. The study concludes with a detailed analysis of the algorithm's security properties and potential applications within the broader context of data security.

title: Title: Quantum Chaos Dynamics – Emergent Information Extraction
abstract: Quantum Chaos Dynamics (QCD) represents a fascinating and increasingly active area of research, exploring the potential of quantum systems to exhibit complex, unpredictable behavior. This paper investigates the design of a self-regulating quantum system capable of extracting and propagating information about chaotic dynamics through entangled states, creating a feedback loop. We propose a novel quantum entanglement protocol that leverages the inherent instability of quantum systems to generate complex, evolving patterns, forcing the system to 'learn' and 'encode' information. The core claim is that this approach offers a pathway to understanding consciousness or advanced computation, a goal previously considered firmly within the realm of theoretical physics. This work begins with a detailed theoretical framework exploring the principles of quantum entanglement and its application to information extraction. It then outlines the architecture of the proposed system, emphasizing the critical role of instability in driving the system's learning process. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit
abstract: Quantum circuit design presents a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of quantum systems. Traditional methods rely heavily on expert knowledge and often struggle to efficiently explore the vast design space. This paper introduces an adaptive quantum circuit, a novel approach that leverages machine learning to dynamically adjust circuit parameters and structure based on input data characteristics, ultimately improving circuit performance and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around a machine learning model trained to learn and optimize circuit design through data analysis. This research explores the potential of this technique to overcome limitations of conventional circuit design and pave the way for more efficient and adaptable quantum systems. The study focuses on the implementation of a specific adaptive circuit design for a simplified quantum system, demonstrating its effectiveness through quantitative analysis.

title: Adaptive Quantum Monte Carlo Simulation – Refinement Through Iterative Error Correction
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum Monte Carlo simulation designed to refine results through iterative error correction, leveraging a quantum error correction method. The core concept is to continuously assess and correct errors during the simulation process, improving accuracy and robustness. Traditional Monte Carlo methods often fail to effectively utilize error correction, necessitating a novel approach. This work proposes a method that incorporates a feedback loop, iteratively correcting errors based on quantum error correction principles, resulting in a significantly enhanced simulation fidelity. We detail the implementation of this iterative correction process and present preliminary results demonstrating the potential for improved accuracy compared to existing techniques.

abstract: This paper presents a geometric proof of concept demonstrating the correctness and efficiency of a novel quantum algorithm, tentatively named "Hyper-Correlation Algorithm" (HCA). The core of the proof relies on constructing a formal geometric model that visualizes and analyzes the algorithm's steps, establishing a rigorous foundation for verification and potential practical application. The model, while currently simplified, aims to capture the essential dynamics of the algorithm's operations. We will explore the mathematical framework underpinning the HCA, including key geometric transformations and relationships. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential benefits of this geometric approach to quantum algorithm validation.

title: Dimensional Generalization and Quantum Entanglement: A Novel Approach
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dimensionality generalization and quantum entanglement to revolutionize the field of quantum computing. We propose a novel model based on the concept of "quantum topology" – a framework that utilizes entangled states to dynamically reshape the geometry of higher-dimensional spaces. This model aims to create new mathematical functions and geometric transformations, offering a pathway to more stable and complex quantum states. The study details the implementation of this approach, examining its implications for quantum computation and the potential for emergent quantum phenomena. The core mechanism hinges on the manipulation of entangled states to define a dynamic, multi-dimensional space, opening avenues for novel mathematical analysis and quantum algorithms.

title: Explainable AI for Reinforcement Learning through Causal Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, from game playing to robotics. However, the "black box" nature of many RL agents presents a significant challenge, particularly in applications where transparency and trust are paramount. This work proposes a novel approach to explainable AI (XAI) within the context of RL by integrating causal reasoning. Traditional RL methods primarily rely on correlation-based learning, which can lead to spurious correlations and opaque decision-making processes. Our approach introduces a mechanism where RL agents explicitly identify and reason about causal relationships between states, actions, and rewards. This allows the agent to articulate *why* it took a particular action, connecting it to the underlying causes of the situation. We formalize this process using a causal Bayesian network and demonstrate how this framework can be implemented within a standard RL architecture. The core contribution is a method for generating explanations that are not only plausible but also reflect a genuine understanding of the environment's causal structure. This framework offers a path towards more robust, trustworthy, and interpretable RL systems, addressing a critical limitation of current approaches.

title: Dynamic Graph Representation Learning with Adaptive Graph Kernels
abstract: Graph representation learning aims to transform raw graph data into meaningful vector representations, enabling downstream tasks like node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed graph kernels, which assume a static graph structure. However, real-world graphs are inherently dynamic, exhibiting evolving node relationships and structural changes over time. This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic graph representation learning that leverages adaptive graph kernels. These kernels dynamically adjust their parameters based on the current graph structure and node interactions, effectively capturing the evolving nature of the graph. We propose a method for generating these adaptive kernels and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and a conceptual exploration. The core contribution lies in providing a flexible and robust approach to graph representation learning that can handle dynamic graph scenarios, addressing a critical limitation of existing methods. Our adaptive kernel approach offers a significant improvement over static kernels by allowing the representation to shift with changes in the underlying graph.

title: Quantum Entanglement Analysis and Manipulation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to classical information theory. This research delves into the analysis and manipulation of quantum entanglement, specifically exploring its potential for instantaneous information transfer and quantum communication. We propose a novel framework for measuring and manipulating entanglement, leveraging its non-local properties to achieve a paradigm shift in information processing. This investigation challenges traditional information theory by demonstrating a potential for bypassing the limitations imposed by locality and causality. The study investigates the implications of this approach on the foundations of information theory, considering its impact on cryptography and distributed quantum computing. This work explores the potential for achieving truly instantaneous communication, a concept previously considered purely theoretical, and examines the impact on our understanding of information's fundamental nature.

title: Biofeedback-Inspired Computation: A Novel Architectural Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational architecture inspired by the feedback mechanisms observed within biological neural systems. The core claim is that mimicking these feedback loops can lead to architectures exhibiting inherent adaptability and robustness – characteristics often lacking in traditional computing paradigms. The proposed architecture leverages feedback signals to dynamically adjust and optimize computational processes. We introduce a formal framework for designing such systems, emphasizing the role of recurrent connections and adaptive weighting schemes. The design incorporates principles from biological neural networks, specifically focusing on mechanisms like synaptic plasticity and error backpropagation. The resulting architecture demonstrates potential advantages in handling complex, dynamic, and noisy data, offering a fundamentally different approach to computation. We present a detailed description of the architecture, including its key components and operational principles, and outline a methodology for its implementation and evaluation. The design aims to bridge the gap between biological intelligence and computational power, providing a foundation for future advancements in intelligent systems.

title: Causal Localization of the Refusal Direction in Audio Language Models
abstract: A large audio language model (LALM) attaches a speech front end to a text language model (LM) that is already safety-aligned. When such a model refuses a harmful spoken request, is the refusal carried by the front end, or inherited from the text LM? We test this with causal interventions. At each model's audio-to-LM interface and at tested LM residual layers, we fit a direction separating harmful from benign prompts, ablate its component, and measure the resulting change in the model's first-token refusal margin. Four of the five models are evaluated under held-out category shift. Across five LALMs spanning three backbone families, with three models passing a baseline safety gate, the largest tested effects occur in a mid-to-late LM band, while ablations of the tested interface directions have little effect. On Qwen2.5-Omni, ablating the L16 direction changes the margin by -7.10, versus -0.013 at the projector. The audio pathway is still in use: zeroing the encoder output changes the margin by -4.7. In the same model, the contrast is linearly decodable at an early layer where single-layer ablation has little effect, and a direction fitted on the LM backbone alone transfers to the full audio model. Because harmful and benign prompts also differ in form, we interpret the direction as refusal-linked rather than harmfulness-specific. These interventions localize dependence of the refusal margin, not where refusal is computed. Moving the margin also does not always change what the model writes. Safety audits of these models should use interventions rather than rely on probes alone, and should examine the inherited text LM alongside the audio interface.

title: MechAudit-40: White-Box Auditing across 40 LLM Attack Mechanisms
abstract: While LLM attacks span prompt optimization, multi-turn context manipulation, retrieval poisoning, and model backdoors, white-box defenses are typically evaluated on isolated attack families. Consequently, whether heterogeneous attacks leave internal representation shifts that generalize to unseen threat mechanisms remains unknown. We present MechAudit-40, a systematic evaluation of 40 attack mechanisms across five open-weight model architectures. Threat-specific success criteria, 100,000 matched clean-attack representation pairs, predefined categories, and grouped holdouts isolate genuine attack-induced displacement from target scale, corpus bias, and data-leakage shortcuts. Across this testbed, attacks induce structured multi-depth trajectories rather than isolated layer spikes. While raw peaks are non-portable across architectures, target-calibrated profiles preserve transferable geometric signatures: under complete mechanism holdout, hidden states alone recover the threat category of unseen attacks with 82.5% accuracy. Guided by this finding, we design MechAudit, a runtime auditor that operates under strict zero-oracle constraints without requiring clean baseline traces or attack metadata. MechAudit detects 81.1% of held-out attack executions at a 0.70% false-positive rate and maintains 78.1% recall when an entire functional category is withheld. In matched comparisons, MechAudit is the only detector that avoids mechanism-level coverage collapse, maintaining over 50% recall across all 40 mechanisms. Internal representations thus support cross-mechanism attack-exposure auditing against calibrated benign references, but decouple from downstream task compromise and parameter integrity.

title: When Retain Constraints Conflict: Mitigating Forget-Retain Interference in Tabular Data
abstract: Machine unlearning aims to remove the influence of designated training data while preserving model utility, but its behavior on tabular data remains underexplored. This gap is important because tabular prediction is widely used in high-stakes domains and is increasingly adapted to language models through record serialization and schema-aware prompting. We identify a key challenge that distinguishes tabular unlearning from unlearning in free-form text or other modalities: schema-induced forget-retain overlap. In serialized tabular data, records share fixed column-name/value slots, similar attribute ranges, and common output spaces. Consequently, a forget row may have nearby retain rows that rely on the same high-signal attributes, causing retain preservation to oppose the update required for forgetting. Motivated by this failure mode, we propose Conflict-Aware Unlearning (CAU), a schema-aware approach that reduces forget-retain interference by relaxing preservation constraints on retained rows that most conflict with the forget set. Across sample-level and feature-level unlearning on clinical and non-medical tabular tasks, CAU more closely matches a retraining oracle while maintaining predictive utility and retain-region behavior. Our results show that reliable tabular LLM unlearning depends not only on the forgetting objective, but also on how retain constraints are constructed.

title: 基于自适应几何的领域扩展算法 (GEA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Geometric Extension Algorithm (GEA), which leverages the principles of geometric topology to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters and facilitate efficient adaptation to diverse field geometries. Traditional parameter tuning methods often involve tedious manual adjustments, while GEA automates this process, resulting in improved algorithm performance and adaptability. The core mechanism of GEA involves transforming algorithm parameters into geometric representations and iteratively adjusting these representations based on the characteristics of the input field. This adaptive adjustment allows the algorithm to effectively 'extend' its capabilities to new and unseen geometric spaces. The paper details the implementation of GEA, provides a rigorous analysis of its performance, and explores its potential applications across various fields.

title: Korpus Paralel Dwibahasa Indonesia–Bali: Dataset Terjemahan Kalimat Lintas Domain
abstract: Korpus paralel dwibahasa yang dirancang secara sistematis untuk mendukung kajian linguistik, penerjemahan berbasis mesin (machine translation), serta pemrosesan bahasa alami (Natural Language Processing / NLP) antara bahasa Indonesia dan bahasa Bali. Dokumen ini merekam korpus teks paralel berskala menengah dengan total entri data valid sebanyak 4.000 pasang kalimat lintas domain. Diorganisasikan ke dalam format tabel empat kolom dengan rincian variabel sebagai berikut: Kolom Indeks ( ): Memuat nomor urut entri data dari baris pertama hingga baris ke-4.000, yang berfungsi sebagai pengenal unik (identifier) untuk setiap pasangan kalimat. Kolom Sumber (Kalimat Bahasa Indonesia): Berisi korpus kalimat rujukan dalam bahasa Indonesia baku maupun semi-formal yang mencakup beragam topik, mulai dari geografi, sejarah, biografi, hingga konteks sosial-budaya modern. Kolom Sasaran (Translasi): Menyajikan hasil terjemahan paralel dari kalimat bahasa Indonesia tersebut ke dalam padanan bahasa Bali yang gramatikal dan kontekstual. Kolom Validasi (Unnamed: 3): Memuat catatan validasi tambahan atau teks pembanding.

title: Title: Adaptive Graph Neural Network Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural network (GNN) structure optimization utilizing an adaptive graph structure adjustment algorithm. Traditional methods often rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability to data variations. This paper introduces a dynamically adjustable structure optimization strategy, leveraging self-tuning algorithms to adjust the network's topology in real-time based on the characteristics of the training data. The proposed method aims to enhance model performance by intelligently adapting the graph's connectivity and node features. The core mechanism involves a self-learning mechanism that dynamically modifies the graph's structure during training, resulting in a more robust and adaptable model. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through experimental results comparing it to existing optimization techniques.

title: Adaptive Modal Neurons
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Adaptive Modal Neurons (AMNs), a novel approach to neural network design inspired by the dynamic modality switching observed in biological neurons. The core claim is that neurons can dynamically adjust their internal modal states based on the characteristics of incoming signals, thereby enhancing their ability to recognize and respond to complex patterns. The proposed mechanism involves designing neurons with variable modal states, utilizing feedback mechanisms and adaptive algorithms to enable learning and adaptation to diverse input patterns. This work explores the theoretical framework and potential applications of AMNs, aiming to improve the robustness and efficiency of artificial neural networks. The key mathematical representation of the core concept is as follows: Let *s1, s2, ..., sK* represent the input signals to the neuron. Let *m1, m2, ..., mN* represent the different modal states of the neuron. The neuron's state *σ* is defined as: *σ = f(s1, s2, ..., sK, m1, m2, ..., mN)* Where *f* is an activation function that governs the transition between modal states. The goal is to design *f* such that *σ* adapts optimally to the input signals. A simplified model update equation would be: *mi = mi + α * (σ - mi) * h(s1, s2, ..., sK)* Where *α* is a learning rate, *h(s1, s2, ..., sK)* is a function representing the input signal's influence on the modal state transition, and *mi* represents the i-th modal state.

title: Dynamically Shaped Neural Architectures via Evolutionary Algorithm
abstract: The design of neural network architectures remains a significant challenge in deep learning, frequently relying on manual expert tuning or predefined templates. This work proposes a novel approach to automatically generate and evolve neural network architectures using an evolutionary algorithm. The core idea is to treat the architecture itself as a population of potential solutions, subject to iterative refinement based on performance and structural constraints. This dynamic shaping capability addresses the limitations of static architectures, which often prove suboptimal for specific datasets. The algorithm iteratively modifies network components – including connections, layers, and activation functions – to achieve enhanced performance. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the evolutionary process and the key considerations for successful implementation. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to create highly adaptive and optimized neural networks, moving beyond traditional design paradigms. The core contribution lies in the automated, data-driven adaptation of network structure, offering a pathway to improved model efficiency and accuracy.

title: Adversarial Training for Secure Federated Learning with Differential Privacy
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, this paradigm is increasingly vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where malicious participants can manipulate the training process to infer sensitive information about individual users. This paper proposes a novel framework combining adversarial training with differential privacy to mitigate these security risks. Our approach trains models robust against attacks aimed at extracting private data while simultaneously guaranteeing differential privacy for each participant. We introduce a modified training loop incorporating adversarial loss alongside the standard FL loss, and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and a conceptual examination. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these two techniques, creating a more secure and privacy-preserving federated learning system. The goal is to provide a foundational approach for building robust FL systems.

title: Adaptive Geometry-Based Machine Learning Hyperparameter Tuning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hyperparameter tuning strategy for machine learning models that leverages geometric structure to optimize model parameters, leading to improved accuracy and generalization. Traditional hyperparameter tuning methods often focus on direct parameter adjustments, while this approach utilizes a geometric representation to guide the optimization process. We propose a framework wherein the model itself is treated as a geometric object, allowing for an adaptive adjustment of parameters based on its inherent structure. The core mechanism involves a dynamic geometric transformation applied to the model's parameters, iteratively refining the model's representation and ultimately leading to better performance. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this geometric approach through a series of experiments on a benchmark dataset, showcasing significant improvements in both accuracy and generalization capabilities compared to conventional hyperparameter tuning techniques.

title: Quantum Spin Adaptive Topology Control
abstract: Quantum spin is a fascinating and weakly interacting quantum system with unique properties, including the ability to exhibit topological phases. These topological phases possess inherent robustness against local perturbations, making them valuable for quantum information processing and quantum technologies. This paper explores the application of quantum spin to adaptive topology control, proposing a novel method leveraging the self-adaptative nature of quantum spin to dynamically adjust the structure of a quantum system, thereby enabling precise control and optimization. Quantum spin provides a unique platform for exploring novel control strategies, potentially surpassing traditional approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed method focuses on utilizing the inherent topological properties of quantum spin to achieve precise manipulation of quantum states. The core claim is that a tailored control mechanism, operating on the self-adaptative behavior of quantum spin, can lead to more precise control of quantum systems. This work addresses the limitations of current control techniques and introduces a fundamentally new approach to topology control.

title: Title: Universal Constraint Mapping via Adaptive Resonance (U-CR)
abstract: The design and application of constraint mapping techniques have been a persistent challenge in mathematical modeling and problem-solving. Traditional methods often struggle with complex constraint structures, limiting their versatility and applicability. This paper introduces U-CR, a novel algorithm for mapping complex constraint structures to a universal mapping, offering a robust framework for creating highly adaptable mathematical models. The core of U-CR lies in the implementation of a dynamically responsive resonance network that adapts to the complexity of constraint mappings. This adaptive mechanism ensures a high degree of flexibility and allows for the creation of models that can readily handle variations in input. This work demonstrates the efficacy of U-CR through a series of theoretical analyses and preliminary implementations, highlighting its potential for revolutionizing the field of constraint mapping.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning for Data-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but its reliance on vast amounts of data often hinders its practical application, particularly within complex and high-dimensional environments. This work introduces a novel approach—Adaptive Meta-Learning for Data-Augmented Reinforcement Learning—that addresses this issue by dynamically adjusting data augmentation strategies during the RL training process. The core idea is to create a meta-learning system that learns to augment data intelligently, guided by the performance feedback of the RL agent. This system iteratively refines its augmentation techniques, aiming to accelerate learning and enhance the agent's robustness. The system utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) to track the learning dynamics and a policy gradient method to optimize the data augmentation strategy. The resulting adaptive data augmentation significantly improves sample efficiency compared to traditional RL methods. The key innovation lies in the closed-loop interaction between data augmentation and RL learning, enabling a truly adaptive and efficient training process. This research contributes to a more practical and scalable RL paradigm by reducing the dependence on massive datasets.

title: Self-Adaptive Probabilistic Field Theory for Quantum Computing Validation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive probabilistic field theory framework for quantum computing validation, aiming to standardize the validation process and enhance the accuracy and reliability of quantum computations. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjustable parameter adjustment strategy, tailored to the unique properties of each quantum system being evaluated. We propose a system that iteratively refines the probability field parameters to optimize the verification process, addressing the limitations of traditional validation methods. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through a theoretical analysis and a preliminary experimental validation. The core claim is that this framework provides a significantly more robust and adaptable validation approach compared to existing methods.

title: Deep Generation Adversarial Networks with Symbolic Reasoning Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge graph understanding and reasoning by fusing deep generation adversarial networks (GANs) with symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the generative capabilities of GANs to create rich representations of knowledge graphs and then utilize symbolic reasoning algorithms to perform logical inference on these representations. The results of the inference are fed back into the GAN to refine its representation learning process. This iterative process aims to enhance the understanding of complex knowledge graphs, addressing limitations of purely statistical or rule-based methods. We introduce a framework combining these two approaches, demonstrating the potential for improved accuracy and interpretability in knowledge graph reasoning. The presented methodology offers a new paradigm for tackling complex reasoning tasks within the knowledge graph domain. ---

title: Adaptive Algorithms Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm design, drawing inspiration from the adaptive mechanisms observed in biological neural networks. The core idea revolves around mimicking the dynamic parameter adjustment capabilities of biological neurons within an algorithmic framework. Specifically, we employ a biologically inspired neural network model, coupled with established machine learning techniques, to create an adaptive algorithm capable of autonomously responding to environmental changes. The resulting system demonstrates a potential for superior performance in dynamic and unpredictable environments compared to traditional, static algorithms. This research offers a new paradigm for optimization, leveraging the inherent robustness and learning abilities of biological systems. The presented framework aims to address challenges in areas such as robotics, control systems, and data analysis, where adaptability is paramount.

title: Probability Space Logic Systems
abstract: Probability Space Logic Systems (P-Space Logic Systems) presents a novel computational paradigm centered around the integration of probabilistic reasoning and logical system analysis. Traditional approaches often struggle with the complexities of high-dimensional and probabilistic scenarios, necessitating a framework that can effectively handle these challenges. This research introduces a system predicated on the construction of a probabilistic space, where logical operations are predicated on probabilistic outcomes, and utilizes probabilistic reasoning to guide the optimization of algorithms. The core mechanism involves embedding logic as a probabilistic process, allowing for dynamic assessment and refinement of algorithm performance through iterative probability evaluation. This approach offers enhanced interpretability and verifiable outcomes compared to traditional methods, particularly when dealing with uncertain or dynamic systems. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this system through a focused examination of algorithm optimization within a simulated high-dimensional probabilistic environment.

title: Causal Graph Generation Algorithms for Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The increasing deployment of complex artificial intelligence (AI) models in critical applications necessitates methods for understanding and explaining their decision-making processes. Traditional model interpretability techniques often struggle to capture the underlying causal relationships driving model predictions, leading to a superficial understanding of how models arrive at their conclusions. This paper proposes a novel algorithm for automatically generating causal graphs from AI models, leveraging techniques of counterfactual reasoning and causal discovery. The core claim is that these generated graphs provide a transparent representation of the causal relationships within the model, significantly enhancing its explainability. The mechanism involves analyzing the relationships between model inputs and outputs using these techniques, resulting in a graph that accurately reflects the model's decision-making logic. We demonstrate a new approach to interpreting complex AI models, increasing their trustworthiness.

title: Topological Protection for Dynamic Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological protection principles to the design of dynamic neural networks. Traditional neural network architectures are vulnerable to neuron failure, leading to diminished performance and limited scalability. This research proposes a novel approach by constructing neural networks with non-trivial topological structures, such as networks connected via Möbius strips, to provide inherent resilience against neuron malfunctions. The core claim is that such architectures significantly reduce the risk of neuron inactivation, leading to robust and scalable learning capabilities. The mechanism relies on utilizing topological protection to ensure network functionality persists even with partial neuron failure. Dynamic adjustment and learning are achieved through simulating neuron interactions and employing topological control. The resulting networks exhibit enhanced robustness and adaptability compared to conventional designs. This work presents a fundamentally new paradigm for neural network architecture, offering a pathway to more reliable and scalable intelligent systems.

title: Directive versus non-directive questions in an LLM-based job interview training
abstract: We examined the structural properties of the interview questions in large language model (LLM)-based systems for job interview training, by a job interview through a role-play simulation using a ChatGPT-based chatbot. The 53 trainees were randomly assigned to one of two groups: 24 trainees to the Directive Questions group, and 29 to the Non-Directive Questions group. Trainees underwent a performance review after the interview and then repeated the job interview simulation. The results demonstrate that trainees in the Directive Questions group invested more time answering each question and had longer training time compared to the Non-Directive Questions group. Responses were longer, and the avatar asked fewer questions, in the second session compared to the first session. Our findings support the hypothesis that LLM-based interviews with directive questions make interviewees think more about each question. In addition, the duration of the response and its length may reflect two different cognitive processes.

title: Which Part of the Context Layer Does the Work? Separating Semantic Content from Retrieval Scaffolding in Text-to-SQL Agents
abstract: Context layers, curated documentation that an analytics agent fetches at query time, produce large accuracy gains on text-to-SQL benchmarks. A with/without comparison cannot say which part of the layer does the work: the semantic content, the retrieval scaffolding that delivers it, or the pre-computed views that usually accompany it. We report a four-arm ablation on DABStep on four models that separates the three. The instrument is a data contract: a YAML artifact that carries a domain's semantics and the rules an agent's tools enforce. One arm empties every field of prose in the frozen contract while holding the tool surface, retrieval instruction, table allow-list and operation rules byte-for-byte fixed. Compiling the contract's own SQL expressions into views gives the ceiling a pre-computed layer would reach: gold on all 176 tasks it covers. Content dominates. It raises hard-task accuracy from 13.9% to 55.1%, 22.6% to 56.6%, 22.9% to 68.4% and 37.0% to 77.4%, beating the same knowledge pasted into the prompt on every model. Scaffolding without content is worth 0 to 5 points on two flash models and 14 to 15 on two frontier models. Against the compiled ceiling the contract arm's shortfall is a failure to derive, and it falls from 39 points to 5 with model capability. The contract beats the prompt because the rule it needs is one lookup away rather than buried in a long prompt: its SQL carries the fee semantics up to 98% of the time against the prompt arm's 4%, and at the lowest cost per correct answer on three of four models. For practitioners: semantics first, scaffolding second, pre-computed macros only where an agent demonstrably fails to derive. Ungoverned arms submitted 166 mutating statements; governed arms none. The gain is confined to the contract's domain. On one model the benchmark's own withheld golds grade the contract arm at 51.9% against 18.8% for the prompt baseline.

title: Beyond QA Matching: Perturbation-Response Fingerprinting via Probability Distributions for Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models are often instruction-tuned, specialized, quantized, or otherwise transformed, making fine-grained provenance difficult. In this paper, we introduce BReF, a training-free fingerprint that compares how probability distributions over four answer-option labels A/B/C/D move under controlled textual perturbations. For each pair of models, BReF selects 25 jointly responsive probes and compares their perturbation log-ratio (PLR) response directions by global cosine similarity. On a unified benchmark with 34 checkpoints, 22 documented direct-parent relations, and 411 suspect-candidate pairs, BReF retrieves the documented parent in 22/22 cases (MRR=1.0000), with DP-DF AUC 1.0000. Same-family discrimination is harder (DP-SF AUC 0.8969), and paired tests show a significant exact-retrieval gain over a magnitude-only Top-25 control. abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum self-adapted topology for the simulation of chaotic systems. Chaotic systems exhibit inherent sensitivity to initial conditions, making precise and efficient simulation challenging. Quantum computing offers unique capabilities, particularly in parallel processing and the exploration of complex dynamics, which could revolutionize our ability to simulate these systems. We outline the core mechanism, explore the potential benefits, and discuss the challenges associated with this approach. The study emphasizes the importance of quantum self-adapted topology in enhancing the precision of chaotic system dynamics.

title: Quantum Information Fusion via Nonlinear Geometric Programming
abstract: Quantum information fusion is a critical challenge in quantum computing, demanding efficient and robust methods for combining and manipulating quantum states. This paper explores the application of Nonlinear Geometric Programming (LGP) as a novel optimization framework for this process, aiming to enhance both quantum information fusion efficiency and quantum error correction capabilities. We propose a new approach that leverages the inherent geometric properties of LGP to improve the synchronization and entanglement of quantum states, ultimately leading to enhanced computational performance. The core mechanism centers around transforming the optimization process into a geometric structure, allowing for the utilization of geometric constraints to guide quantum state evolution and reduce the impact of noise. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of LGP to significantly improve quantum information fusion.

title: Fractal Recursive Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to Bayesian inference termed "Fractal Recursive Bayesian Inference." The core idea is that Bayesian inference can be effectively implemented through a fractal recursive process, mirroring the self-similar structure of fractals to manage hierarchical and complex data. The method employs a Bayesian inference engine that recursively decomposes the model space into progressively smaller, fractal-like regions, updating beliefs at each level based on local data. This process continues until a global estimate is achieved. The key novelty lies in utilizing fractal geometry as a fundamental structural principle within the Bayesian inference engine, providing a new framework for addressing model complexity and offering potentially improved convergence rates and interpretability compared to traditional approaches. This work establishes a theoretical foundation for this method, outlining the mechanics and potential benefits.

title: Emergent Semantics in Recursive Adaptive Language Models
abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenon of emergent semantics in large language models (LLMs). Traditionally, the emergence of meaning within LLMs has been viewed as a largely stochastic and unpredictable process. We propose a novel framework that posits a more structured mechanism: recursive adaptive feedback. Our core claim is that the semantic richness observed in LLMs isn't purely random but arises from a hierarchical and context-dependent system of self-evaluation and adjustment. We introduce a recursive neural network architecture where the model's weights are dynamically modified based on assessments of the current linguistic context and the generated output. This feedback loop creates a system capable of learning and refining its internal representation of meaning over time. We demonstrate, through a conceptual model and mathematical formulation, that this recursive adaptive process can explain observed emergent behaviors, shifting the perspective from a purely probabilistic view to a controllable, rule-governed one. The key mathematical components involve the definition of a loss function that incorporates both contextual similarity and output coherence, and the iterative application of gradient descent to optimize the model's parameters. This work lays the groundwork for a deeper understanding of how meaning can be systematically generated within LLMs and suggests potential avenues for enhancing their semantic capabilities.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Cooperative and Competitive Strategies using Hierarchical Temporal Action Planning
abstract: This paper explores the application of Hierarchical Temporal Action Planning (HTAP) within Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to facilitate more complex and adaptive behaviors in cooperative and competitive scenarios. Traditional MARL approaches often struggle with scalability and coordination, particularly when agents must dynamically shift between collaborative and competitive strategies. Our approach introduces a hierarchical system where agents learn to decompose tasks into temporally extended action sequences, managed by a shared temporal plan. This plan explicitly balances cooperative and competitive objectives, allowing agents to engage in sophisticated, dynamically adjusted interactions. The core claim is that this combination of HTAP and MARL enables the development of multi-agent systems capable of exhibiting more nuanced and adaptive behavior. We present a framework for implementing this system and outline its potential for addressing complex challenges in diverse multi-agent environments. The key innovation lies in the structured, temporally-aware coordination achieved through the hierarchical planning, moving beyond simple agent interactions to create truly dynamic and responsive multi-agent teams.

title: 基于量子纠缠的几何验证与预测
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar quantum phenomenon, offers a potentially revolutionary approach to geometry and modeling. This paper explores the application of entanglement to validate and predict geometric models, aiming for unprecedented accuracy through enhanced computational capabilities. We propose a novel framework that utilizes entangled states to analyze geometric properties, offering a pathway to fundamentally improve the precision of geometric constructions. This work leverages the unique characteristics of entanglement to provide a new method for validating physical models and achieving high-fidelity geometric representations. The core mechanism centers around the exploration of entanglement-induced correlations within geometric data, providing a robust and potentially transformative methodology. The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the implications and potential future directions for this innovative approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm Verification via Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel methodology for algorithm verification leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics through sophisticated classical simulations. The core idea centers on mimicking quantum phenomena such as superposition and interference within a simulated environment to rigorously test computationally demanding algorithms, especially those dealing with complex probability distributions. Traditional algorithm verification often relies on exhaustive testing or statistical sampling, which may fail to uncover subtle errors arising from numerical inaccuracies or deviations from expected probabilistic behavior. Our approach utilizes advanced simulation techniques to generate probabilistic outputs that closely resemble those produced by the algorithm under test, thereby exposing hidden errors undetectable by conventional methods. We demonstrate, theoretically, how this approach can improve the reliability and confidence in the correctness of algorithms, especially those where verification is challenging due to the scale of computations or the complexity of the underlying probability models. The method offers a pathway to a more robust and comprehensive verification process, aligning with the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics.

title: Self-Adaptive Topology for Quantum Information Storage Protocols
abstract: Quantum information storage is a significant challenge due to the fragility of quantum states. This paper explores the use of self-adaptive topology as a core mechanism to enhance the storage and retrieval efficiency of quantum information. We propose a novel protocol that dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum system to optimize performance, leveraging computational predictions to guide future optimization efforts. This approach offers a departure from traditional methods, promising to overcome limitations in current storage strategies. The paper details the design of the adaptive topology mechanism, its implementation within a quantum state, and the resulting efficiency gains observed through simulations and analyses. We conclude by highlighting the potential of this methodology for advancing quantum information technologies.

title: Graph-Based Bayesian Inference for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its performance often degrades significantly when faced with incomplete observability – situations where the agent lacks full information about the environment's state. Traditional RL algorithms struggle to effectively handle this uncertainty, leading to suboptimal policies and unreliable behavior. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging graph-based Bayesian inference to address this challenge. We construct a graph representation of the environment, where nodes represent states, actions, and the inherent uncertainties associated with each. By applying Bayesian inference directly on this graph, we enable the agent to update its belief about the environment and, subsequently, optimize its policy in a principled manner. The key innovation lies in the explicit modeling of uncertainty and the resulting efficient reasoning capabilities, providing a substantial advantage over conventional RL methods, particularly in partially observable environments. This framework offers a pathway towards more robust and reliable RL agents capable of operating effectively in real-world scenarios characterized by incomplete information.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed memory optimization leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to utilize entanglement for direct data sharing and collaborative computation between distant computing nodes, circumventing the limitations imposed by classical communication. We establish a distributed network composed of entangled qubits, enabling instantaneous data transfer and synchronization through manipulation of the entangled state. This mechanism facilitates efficient distributed memory operations and parallel execution of complex computations. The potential of this approach to drastically improve distributed memory performance is explored, representing a significant step towards realizing "quantum distributed memory." The theoretical framework and key concepts are presented, outlining a foundational methodology for future research and development in this field. This work focuses on the theoretical aspects of entanglement-based distributed memory, without experimental validation.
