title: Used, Mentioned, or Condemned? A Controlled Contrast-Set Diagnostic for the Use-Mention Distinction in Code-Mixed Hinglish Misogyny Detection
abstract: Lexicon-driven misogyny detectors cannot, by construction, distinguish a slur used against a woman from the same slur mentioned in counter-speech ("don't call her that") -- yet exactly this distinction governs whether moderation protects or silences the people discussing abuse. We study this problem in code-mixed Hinglish and make three contributions. First, we diagnose two evaluation artifacts on a publicly available redacted corpus: category-encoding anonymization placeholders leak the label (a no-learning rule scores 1.000), and even after they are neutralized misogynistic and benign comments occupy lexically disjoint registers, so bag-of-words reaches macro-F1 approximately 1.00 under random cross-validation but collapses under template-disjoint evaluation. Second, we release Hinglish-MGY-Diag, a deterministic generator and a 416-item / 163-minimal-pair contrast-set diagnostic across five linguistically motivated categories in which slur presence and gendered register are decorrelated from the label by construction. Third, we introduce a strict pair-consistency metric that credits a model only when both members of a minimal pair are correctly labelled. Five from-scratch classical baselines evaluated under construction-disjoint five-fold cross-validation reveal that the strongest model reaches 0.93 accuracy on the cleanest use-mention subset but only 0.82 consistency -- it still mislabels roughly one counter-speech pair in five. A frontier LLM used as an author-model ceiling attains 1.000 on all metrics, doubling as independent label validation and confirming the benchmark is a capability gradient rather than an adversarial wall. We release all code, data, the generator, and an arms-length LLM harness for reproducing every number.

title: SAGE: A Hierarchical Framework for Evaluating Interpretive Literary Quality in Narratives
abstract: Assessing the literary quality of narratives requires evaluating interpretive dimensions (cultural representation, emotional depth, and philosophical engagement) that existing NLG metrics cannot measure. We introduce SAGE, a six-layer evaluation framework that separates rule-based assessment of observable textual properties from LLM-based evaluation of interpretive qualities drawn from cultural theory, affect theory, and existentialist philosophy. Each interpretive layer is assessed through multi-round iterative LLM evaluation with independent cross-validation, achieving measurement-grade reliability (98.8% convergence, >94% inter-rater agreement) stable across evaluator models. Validated on 600 evaluations across 100 short stories, our central finding is a systematic capability boundary: emotional-psychological representation approaches human levels, while cultural critique and philosophical depth exhibit approximately double the gap. LLM-generated narratives score below even commercial genre fiction on all three layers. We interpret this as a boundary between pattern-reproducible literary capacities learnable from training corpora and stance-requiring ones demanding cultural positioning and philosophical engagement that pattern matching alone cannot provide.

title: The Adaptive Learning Framework Based on Graph-Based Machine Learning
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive learning framework for machine learning that automatically adjusts model parameters to enhance model performance. Traditional machine learning methods often lack the ability to dynamically adjust parameters based on data, limiting their effectiveness. This work introduces a novel approach leveraging graph structure to intelligently optimize model parameters, leading to improved accuracy and generalization. The framework employs a hierarchical graph representation to capture complex relationships within the data, facilitating automated parameter tuning. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through extensive experiments on various datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model performance compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism lies in the utilization of graph-based optimization techniques to systematically refine parameter values.

title: Quantum Entanglement Analysis and Anti-Decoy Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to classical physics and has captivated researchers for decades. This paper investigates the concept of non-locality, specifically its connection to entanglement, and proposes a novel framework for analyzing quantum entanglement through a process called "Entanglement Anti-Decoy" (EAD). The core aim is to design an algorithm capable of reverse entanglement, offering a potential path towards quantum information processing. This research explores the implications of this approach, highlighting its potential to overcome the limitations of traditional quantum computation and provide a new avenue for exploring the mysteries of quantum entanglement. We will detail the proposed EAD algorithm, its underlying mathematical principles, and its potential to facilitate the development of robust quantum communication protocols. The paper will conclude with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm optimization strategy based on dynamic topology. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting quantum parameters during the execution of quantum algorithms, leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures to enhance algorithm performance and stability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing significant improvements compared to existing static optimization techniques. The paper also discusses the theoretical underpinnings of this dynamic topology approach and its potential implications for the design and implementation of advanced quantum algorithms. The resulting optimization strategy promises to unlock new capabilities and enhance the reliability of quantum computations.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Phase Field Modeling
abstract: Quantum-enhanced phase field modeling presents a novel approach to predicting the behavior of materials under thermal and mechanical stress, aiming to significantly improve the accuracy of simulations compared to traditional methods. This paper details a new algorithmic framework leveraging quantum computation to accelerate the solution of phase field equations, addressing the computational bottleneck inherent in this modeling discipline. We explore the potential of quantum-enhanced iterative solvers to achieve substantial speedups and improved precision, ultimately offering a pathway toward more efficient and reliable material characterization. This work presents a rigorous theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this methodology.

title: 基于动态量子态的量子电路设计
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit design based on the dynamic evolution of quantum states. Traditional quantum circuit design often relies on static circuits, limiting design possibilities. We propose a method that leverages the inherent dynamism of quantum states to optimize circuit performance and enhance quantum computation. The core mechanism involves learning the dynamic state transformation and employing it to control the circuit's output. This dynamic adaptation allows for more efficient and flexible quantum circuit design. The proposed method offers a promising path towards achieving greater computational power and exploring novel quantum algorithms. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components and potential advantages of this dynamic quantum circuit design.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel graph-based learning algorithm based on adaptive deep learning. Traditional graph-based learning methods often rely on predefined graph structures, limiting their flexibility and adaptability. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the graph structure parameters to optimize the learning process, resulting in improved model performance and efficiency. We present a framework for automated graph construction and parameter optimization, focusing on enhancing the model's ability to capture complex relationships within the data. The core mechanism involves a reinforcement learning-inspired approach to adjust the graph's connectivity and edge weights, leading to a more robust and efficient learning process. We evaluate the algorithm's performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in various graph-related tasks. The research highlights the potential of adaptive graph learning to address challenges in traditional graph-based methods.

title: Quantum Particle Physics Simulation
abstract: Quantum particle physics simulation is a rapidly evolving field with the potential to revolutionize our understanding of fundamental physics. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum simulation framework leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and superposition to model complex phenomena, including nuclear fusion and particle interactions. We propose a new approach to simulation that utilizes quantum algorithms to accurately predict previously unobserved physical states. The core claim is that this framework will significantly advance our ability to explore the limits of quantum mechanics and potentially uncover new physics. The paper details the framework's design, implementation of key quantum algorithms, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in simulating specific scenarios.

abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to quantum computation utilizing adaptive geometric topology transformations. We propose a novel algorithm based on quantum entanglement that allows for the dynamic reshaping of quantum states, offering a pathway towards enhanced computational capabilities. The core of this system lies in the strategic application of quantum entanglement to induce and control topological transformations within the quantum state space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations of traditional methods in specific quantum computation scenarios. This research explores the inherent advantages of leveraging entanglement for geometric manipulation, paving the way for more flexible and powerful quantum algorithms.

title: Title: Non-Local Topological Field Theory (NTFT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for non-local topological field theory, aiming to overcome limitations in current quantum entanglement models. Traditional entanglement concepts often struggle with long-range effects, hindering the development of robust quantum information processing. NTFT proposes a radical shift, introducing a 'topological field' that facilitates instantaneous information transmission across distances, fundamentally altering the landscape of quantum computation. We explore the theoretical implications of this approach, detailing the core mechanism of information transfer and outlining a preliminary model for its application. The proposed theory offers a potential pathway to achieve truly global quantum information processing, exceeding the capabilities of conventional entanglement techniques.

title: Title: Zero-Assisted Geometric Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel zero-assistance geometric optimization algorithm designed to overcome the limitations of traditional optimization techniques, particularly in the presence of complex, high-dimensional search spaces. The core concept revolves around incorporating a probabilistic exploration strategy that allows the algorithm to escape local minima and discover optimal solutions even in regions classically considered inaccessible. We propose a mechanism that iteratively assesses the "assistance" required to continue exploration, dynamically adjusting the level of support to achieve efficient convergence. title: Quantum Simulation of Dynamical Systems with Adaptive Noise
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a novel approach to modeling complex dynamical systems, particularly those exhibiting intricate dynamics and sensitivity to initial conditions. This paper explores a quantum algorithm designed to accurately simulate such systems with adaptive noise. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the noise level based on the system's state, a departure from traditional approaches that treat noise as a constant. We detail the algorithm's design, theoretical analysis, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating improved predictive power compared to classical simulations. The goal is to significantly enhance the fidelity and robustness of dynamical system modeling, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum mechanics.

title: Active Learning-based Machine Learning Model Training
abstract: This paper investigates the application of active learning techniques to enhance the training efficiency and accuracy of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning model training frequently relies on random sample selection, which can be highly inefficient, particularly when dealing with large datasets where the majority of data points may not contribute significantly to model improvement. Active learning provides a framework for intelligently selecting the most informative samples for annotation, thereby reducing the annotation burden while maximizing model performance. The core claim of this work is that by strategically utilizing active learning methods to prioritize sample selection based on uncertainty or information gain, we can significantly improve the training efficiency and overall predictive accuracy of machine learning models. We propose a novel active learning strategy based on model uncertainty quantification and information gain estimation. This approach aims to identify samples where the model is most uncertain or where labeling would provide the greatest information for model refinement. The methodology utilizes a core mechanism of constructing an active learning policy, offering a targeted approach to annotation, ultimately leading to more effective model training.

title: HE-CloudML: a privacy-preserving framework for secure machine learning inference over encrypted cloud data using homomorphic encryption
abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of cloud-based Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) exposes sensitive user data to critical privacy risks during inference, as plaintext data must typically be processed by untrusted cloud servers. This paper presents HE-CloudML, a unified privacy-preserving framework for secure deep neural network (DNN) inference over encrypted cloud data using Homomorphic Encryption (HE). HE-CloudML is architected as a three-tier system comprising a client-side CKKS encryption module, a cloud-side HE inference engine, and a distributed key management layer, ensuring that raw input data is never exposed to the server at any stage of computation. The framework introduces HE-compatible polynomial activation function approximations via degree-5 Chebyshev minimax polynomials, an optimized SIMD ciphertext batching strategy exploiting Ring Learning With Errors (RLWE) slot packing, and an adaptive lazy bootstrapping pipeline to substantially reduce homomorphic evaluation depth and inference latency. A formal security analysis under the IND-CPA model grounded in the RLWE hardness assumption demonstrates resistance to inference, model inversion, and membership inference attacks. Comprehensive experiments across three domains benchmark image classification (MNIST: 99.28%, CIFAR-10: 90.37%), medical imaging (93.61%), and financial fraud detection (96.44%) demonstrate that HE-CloudML achieves near-plaintext accuracy with a maximum accuracy drop of 1.81%, while delivering up to 26.9× latency improvements over CryptoNets.

title: CAMFT: Conflict-Aware Mergeable Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models
abstract: Model merging has emerged as a promising paradigm for integrating multiple task-specific capabilities into a single large language model. However, existing methods predominantly focus on post-hoc processing of independently fine-tuned models, overlooking how the training phase itself impacts cross-task compatibility. Resolving parameter conflicts after fine-tuning is inherently sub-optimal. To address this, we propose CAMFT, a Conflict-Aware Mergeable Fine-Tuning method that makes task adaptation both efficient and mergeaware. CAMFT treats mergeability as a property shaped during fine-tuning, rather than only a problem to be solved after fine-tuning. By guiding each task to update sparse coordinates with lower cross-task conflict, CAMFT produces task updates that are efficient to train and more compatible for downstream model merging. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CAMFT outperforms standard finetuning baselines in multi-task merging scenarios. Codes are available at https://github.com/gyanchow/CAMFT-LLM.

title: Efficient Hardware Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing
abstract: Register-Transfer Level (RTL) simulation is widely used to test hardware before it is fabricated. To allow testing for security related information flow properties, such as confidentiality and integrity, taint logic can be automatically added to the design to track how information flows through it. However, taint logic instrumented by the state-of-the-art, such as CellIFT, makes simulation-based testing prohibitively expensive: On our evaluation of Mega-BOOM (136K cells), it increases the instrumented design to 5.81x the original cell count and causes a 143.72x simulation slowdown. The taint logic could be simplified to improve simulation speed, but it will inevitably trade off its precision. This lightweight, imprecise taint logic will introduce false positives and may eventually result in even more overhead to check these false positives. This paper explores the research question of where precision is actually needed in the design to overcome the overhead of false positives. It presents CEGAR-T, a framework that automatically synthesizes taint logic that minimizes the taint-logic instrumentation overhead while guaranteeing no false positives (relative to the precise CellIFT baseline). We have implemented CEGAR-T and evaluated it on the safe instruction set problem for timing side-channel security across open-source RISC-V cores. Over all evaluated cores, CEGAR-T reduces both instrumentation and simulation overhead, in geometric-mean, from 5.64x to 1.42x and from 34.65x to 1.79x, respectively, without compromising the precision benefit of the CellIFT baseline.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Universal Computation Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate no matter how far apart they are, has emerged as a potentially transformative force in quantum computing. This paper explores the feasibility of utilizing quantum entanglement as a core mechanism for creating a universal computational model, capable of tackling complex calculations across diverse quantum systems. We propose a novel approach that leverages entanglement to establish a fundamentally different computational paradigm, moving beyond the limitations of classical computation. The core claim of this research is that a well-designed quantum entanglement-based computational framework can enable computations that are fundamentally impossible for classical computers. This work details the proposed model, its underlying principles, and potential applications across various computational domains.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for computation exceeding the capabilities of classical systems. This work addresses a critical challenge in quantum computing, focusing on the potential of non-linear models to unlock new optimization strategies.

title: Rank Aware Strategic Policy Design for Language Based Economic Environments
abstract: Games in Language Based Economic Environments (GLEE) evaluates language agents in multiround bargaining, bilateral negotiation, and repeated persuasion. We report an agent that finished second in the 2026 agent track at a rating of 2590.02 after 46,564 officially rated games. Because GLEE ranks payoffs within each configuration and role, maximizing expected money need not maximize the competition score. Our final policy combines game-theoretic benchmarks, fitted opponent-response models, and history-based rules without a language model at inference. Bargaining balances discounted continuation against agreement risk; negotiation separates visible-surplus decisions from hidden-value inference; persuasion uses recommendations, observed quality, and credibility to guide purchases. We trace the development and failures of these strategies. A separate 245-game final-policy audit connects 2,288 returned actions to authenticated replays. Agreement alone was insufficient: all 15 bargaining games in which a rank-proxy rule changed offers agreed, yet 14 lost rating. These results describe a competitive system, not individual component effects.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Theory: An Adaptive Gaussian Field Theory
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibiting correlations that defy classical intuition. This research investigates the use of an adaptive Gaussian field theory to construct a robust model for quantum entanglement information theory. This model aims to provide more accurate simulations of entanglement properties and precise measurement/control capabilities, particularly within the context of quantum computing and quantum communication. The core mechanism involves integrating Gaussian field theory with the mathematical description of entanglement, allowing for dynamic adaptation of the entanglement state to environmental fluctuations. This approach offers a significant advancement in our understanding and manipulation of quantum entanglement. The paper demonstrates the model's ability to capture complex entanglement behaviors and provides a framework for advanced quantum algorithms and secure communication protocols.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction (QECS)
abstract: This paper introduces Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction (QECS), a novel algorithm designed to accelerate the solution of complex optimization problems using quantum annealing. Traditional constraint satisfaction algorithms often struggle with large, high-dimensional search spaces, limiting their effectiveness. QECS leverages quantum annealing to efficiently explore the solution space, potentially offering exponential speedups compared to classical methods. The core mechanism centers on using quantum annealing to identify and exploit local optima, significantly reducing the computational cost of finding optimal solutions. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its potential for substantial improvements in optimization tasks across diverse problem domains.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Bayesian Knowledge Graphs
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to programming – Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Bayesian Knowledge Graphs (KNP) – designed to overcome the limitations of traditional neural networks and symbolic AI systems. The core idea is to create a synergistic system that leverages the pattern recognition abilities of neural networks and the logical deduction capabilities of symbolic reasoning, mediated by a Bayesian Knowledge Graph. The system learns to translate raw data into symbolic representations, which are then utilized within the KGP for probabilistic inference and the generation of executable symbolic programs. This iterative process continuously refines both the neural representation and the underlying symbolic knowledge, leading to a dynamically adapting reasoning engine. We present a detailed framework for the KNP, emphasizing the Bayesian component and its role in enabling robust and flexible programming. The system's architecture, incorporating a neural network for feature extraction and a Bayesian Knowledge Graph for inference and program generation, represents a significant advancement in the field of neuro-symbolic AI. Ultimately, this work demonstrates a pathway towards more intelligent and adaptable AI systems capable of handling complex, real-world problems.

title: Explainable AI via Causal Mediation Analysis of Neural Network Predictions
abstract: The increasing deployment of neural networks in critical applications necessitates methods for understanding their decision-making processes – a field often referred to as Explainable AI (XAI). Traditional XAI techniques frequently provide post-hoc explanations that lack a solid causal foundation, potentially masking spurious correlations and leading to misleading interpretations. This paper proposes a novel approach to XAI that leverages causal mediation analysis to uncover the underlying causal pathways driving neural network predictions. We treat the neural network's prediction as a mediator variable, allowing us to rigorously assess the relationships between input features and the target variable through this intermediary. This framework provides a more robust and interpretable explanation by explicitly considering causal mechanisms. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical exploration and illustrate its benefits with a simplified example. The core claim of this work is that causal mediation analysis significantly enhances the explainability of neural network predictions by revealing the true causal influences.

title: Quantum Computing Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but realizing this potential requires sophisticated algorithms for parameter optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum systems, particularly when dealing with large, multi-dimensional parameter spaces. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing algorithm, the Quantum Parameter Adjustment Algorithm (QPAA), designed to address these challenges by dynamically analyzing quantum process to automatically adjust parameters, thereby enhancing both computational efficiency and accuracy. This algorithm leverages machine learning techniques to achieve self-adaptive parameter correction, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum optimization. We provide a detailed explanation of the algorithm's core mechanisms, including the dynamic analysis framework and the machine learning component, and discuss the potential benefits and limitations of this approach.

title: #基于生物神经网络的自适应控制系统 (BNAC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Adaptive Control System based on Biological Neural Networks (BNAC), aiming to address the limitations of conventional control systems regarding adaptability and robustness. The core concept of BNAC lies in mimicking the self-organizing capabilities observed in biological neural networks. Specifically, we leverage a Pulse Neural Network (PNN) architecture and utilize synaptic plasticity – the ability of synapses to strengthen or weaken over time – to enable adaptive control strategies. This approach allows the system to dynamically adjust its control parameters in response to changes in the environment. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the PNN model and the plasticity rules. The key novelty of BNAC resides in its direct emulation of biological neural network adaptation, promising enhanced resilience and performance in complex control scenarios. We demonstrate the theoretical framework and outline a potential implementation strategy for BNAC systems.

title: Neural Evolution Network (NEN)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design and optimization, termed the Neural Evolution Network (NEN). The core concept of NEN involves integrating the principles of neural networks with evolutionary algorithms, specifically utilizing a genetic algorithm to dynamically optimize both the network's architecture and the connections between neurons. Traditional methods for neural network design often rely on manual tuning and expert knowledge, leading to suboptimal performance. NEN addresses this limitation by introducing a self-adaptive evolutionary process. title: Algorithmic Stability Analysis via Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Algorithmic stability analysis in distributed systems is a critical aspect of ensuring correct and reliable operation, particularly as systems grow in complexity and scale. However, traditional methods for assessing stability – often relying on exhaustive simulation – quickly become computationally infeasible due to the exponential growth of possible system states. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging abstract interpretation techniques to address this challenge. We demonstrate how abstract models can be derived from distributed algorithms, enabling efficient analysis of stability properties without the need for full-scale simulations. Our methodology provides a scalable solution for analyzing algorithmic stability, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. The core claim is that analyzing algorithmic stability is computationally intractable. The core mechanism involves applying abstract interpretation to derive abstract models, facilitating efficient stability analysis. This approach represents a new way to tackle the problem, offering a scalable solution.

abstract: This paper explores the development and implementation of an adaptive algorithm leveraging bioelectrochemical feedback for improved performance. We establish a mapping between bioelectrical signal characteristics and algorithm performance, enabling a truly adaptive and intelligent system. The research highlights the potential for creating more robust and responsive algorithms across diverse applications where real-time adaptation is crucial.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Large-Scale Machine Learning Models
abstract: The training of large-scale machine learning models presents significant computational challenges, primarily due to the inherent complexity of optimization algorithms like stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its variants. These algorithms often struggle with convergence speed, getting trapped in local minima, and the ability to effectively explore the vast solution space. This paper investigates the potential of quantum-inspired optimization techniques to address these limitations. Specifically, we explore the application of quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approaches to accelerate the training and optimization process of large-scale machine learning models. Our core claim is that by mapping the optimization problem to a quantum system, we can leverage quantum computation to overcome the computational bottlenecks associated with classical optimization methods. We propose a framework where the objective function of the machine learning model is translated into a Hamiltonian for a quantum annealer or the cost function for a VQE, enabling a quantum-inspired solution. The results, while theoretical in this initial exploration, demonstrate a potential pathway for significantly reducing training times and improving the overall performance of large-scale machine learning models. Further research is needed to develop efficient hybrid quantum-classical algorithms and explore the practical limitations of this approach.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Models: Leveraging Causal Inference for Enhanced Interpretability and Reliability
abstract: This paper investigates the application of causal inference techniques to enhance the interpretability and reliability of deep learning models. Traditional deep learning models often operate as black boxes, lacking transparency and making it difficult to understand the reasoning behind their predictions. We propose a framework that integrates causal reasoning into the model architecture and inference process. This framework aims to identify and utilize the underlying causal relationships within the data and model, thereby providing more meaningful and trustworthy explanations. Specifically, we explore methods for detecting spurious correlations and disentangling causal influences. The core claim of this research is that leveraging causal inference significantly improves both the interpretability and the robustness of deep learning models. Our approach offers a pathway towards building more reliable and trustworthy AI systems, addressing a critical limitation of current deep learning technology. The presented methodology provides a structured approach for incorporating causal reasoning, ultimately leading to models that are not only accurate but also explainable.

title: Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself, and What a Falling Score Actually Measures
abstract: "An agent that writes its conclusions into a store it later retrieves from closes a loop usually reported as one-way contamination. Taking the loop to the infinite-tenure limit against an append-only store gives a different picture: because writing never deletes, the reachable state space has a hard upper edge at (n-1)/n, so the outcome is a choice between two edges rather than a decay. At f_0 = 0.9 the interval between the two modes holds 3.6% of 220 runs where a uniform spread would put 20.6%, and is strictly empty on the first 15; the pooled mean describes 8.2% of the runs it summarises, the median 68.2%. Everything the model contributes is carried by one measured primitive with no fitted parameter, the copy function γ(ϕ): on 36 Wikidata facts, sign(\hatγ - γ_{crit}), with γ_{crit} = 1/k at r = 0, w = 1, predicts the direction of drift on 353 of 360 real-fact runs (39 of 40 synthetic in the same batch). Scale does not rescue the store: pooled frontier capture is 0.850, with claude-sonnet-4.5 captured on 20 of 20 seeds against our registered prediction of <0.5. What the interval tests is distinguishability rather than count: on the real facts, multi-valued runs have 6.4x its occupancy of the rest. It survives at f_0 in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5}, capture peaks at f_0 = 0.5, and of four interventions with criteria frozen first, timing dominates fraction at matched budget while a consistency gate drives every model to 0.993. The resampling unit is the seed, at a design effect of 3.75 on a pooled level: under a 44-seed control the ordering supporting claim 4 collapses from Spearman +0.98 at three seeds to +0.31-0.80 at forty-four, while claim 2's ordering is exact there (+1.00, p = 0.017). All 87 graded rows are in Appendix W, 37 of them graded withdrawn, failed, self-correcting, undecidable or an acknowledged limit, against 50 that are not."

title: Computation and Applications of Euclidean and Normed Representations of Massive Data
abstract: This thesis investigates Euclidean-space and $\ell_p$-norm representations of different forms of data, with a focus on efficient algorithms for computing these representations in settings where the amount of data is very large. The applications of such representations are also discussed: they may be used to summarize the data in a more compact form for downstream tasks while preserving its most salient properties; and further, they may also be used to extract insights about the data that may not be apparent in its original form. This thesis presents novel algorithms for computing Euclidean representations in the case where the data comes with linear structure, as well as in the case where the data comes only with metric, or distance structure. In addition, we give algorithms for computing $\ell_p$-norm representations in linear structured cases. The analyses of these algorithms use tools from geometry, probability, and optimization, and these tools are used to illuminate other algorithms for similar problems.

abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive optimization algorithm for algorithmic parameter tuning, leveraging the power of graph-based adaptation. The core innovation lies in utilizing a graph structure to automatically adjust algorithm parameters, significantly enhancing the algorithm's adaptability and performance across diverse datasets and problem domains. The algorithm's architecture is designed to dynamically adjust parameters based on observed data patterns, resulting in improved convergence speed, robustness, and generalization capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimental validation across multiple optimization tasks, showcasing substantial improvements in both accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional optimization techniques.

title: Probability Space Variable Adaptive Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel learning algorithm for probability space variables that dynamically adjusts weights based on data distribution shifts. The algorithm, termed Adaptive Weight Adjustment (AWA), leverages a mechanism to continuously re-evaluate and optimize weights based on observed data patterns. The core principle is to maintain a set of weighted probabilities representing the data, and iteratively adjust these weights to improve predictive accuracy and model robustness. The proposed AWA addresses limitations of existing approaches by providing a mechanism for continuous weight adaptation, allowing the algorithm to effectively handle complex data landscapes. We present a comprehensive implementation and analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of AWA in various scenarios, achieving superior performance compared to existing methods.

title: Title: Algorithmic Constraint Optimization for Chaos-Driven Systems
abstract: This paper investigates algorithmic constraint optimization techniques for chaotic systems, aiming to generate robust and unpredictable behavior. Traditional constraint optimization methods often fail to adequately address the inherent instability of such systems, necessitating a novel approach. We propose a self-learning evolutionary algorithm that dynamically refines constraints through reinforcement learning, focusing on minimizing a "chaos score" – a measure of instability – to produce highly resilient and unpredictable solutions. The algorithm systematically analyzes the system's dynamics, iteratively adjusting constraints to achieve optimal stability and novelty. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed method, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating complex, self-organizing behavior within a variety of chaotic systems.

abstract: High-dimensional domain dynamics models (HDDM) pose significant challenges in fields such as biology and medicine due to the scarcity of data. HDDM leverages an adaptive learning algorithm to efficiently learn and adapt to data, particularly in complex, high-dimensional domains. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of simulations and analyses focusing on biological system modeling. The core mechanism centers on iterative parameter adjustment guided by a learning rate, fostering rapid model adaptation and improved generalization. This work offers a promising approach to overcome data limitations inherent in HDDM applications.

title: Title: Geometric Proofs for Complex Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging geometric concepts to automate the generation of geometric proofs for complex algorithms. The core claim posits the development of a novel system that automatically constructs geometric proofs, significantly reducing the reliance on manual verification. This is achieved through the integration of geometric curves, shapes, and transformations, enabling the verification of complex algorithms through a system of automated geometric constructions. We present a preliminary system demonstrating the feasibility of automated geometric proof generation for a specific, albeit simplified, algorithm. This work represents a significant step towards a more efficient and automated verification process for a broad range of complex algorithms.

title: Topological Regularization for Deep Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of topological regularization to deep learning models, aiming to enhance model stability and robustness. Deep learning models often suffer from sensitivity to initializations and small perturbations, leading to overfitting and poor generalization. We introduce a novel topological regularization term that explicitly penalizes deviations from a predefined topological structure, encouraging more consistent and robust learning. The core mechanism involves constructing a topological graph representing the model's learned representations and then utilizing this graph to guide the optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on benchmark datasets, demonstrating improved generalization performance and reduced sensitivity to hyperparameter tuning. This work offers a principled and structured method for improving the quality of deep learning models.

title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Time Series Prediction with Entangled Reservoirs
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum reservoir computing (QRC) utilizing entangled quantum reservoirs for enhanced time series prediction. Traditional reservoir computing relies on randomly connected recurrent neural networks, often struggling to effectively capture complex temporal dependencies inherent in time series data. We propose a novel approach where the reservoir is replaced by a quantum system, specifically a collection of coupled qubits, governed by quantum interference. The introduction of entanglement within the reservoir is hypothesized to significantly improve its ability to model and predict time series data. Theoretical analysis and simplified models demonstrate a potential for enhanced performance compared to classical reservoir computing methods. The core claim is that entangled quantum reservoirs can achieve superior time series prediction accuracy. This work lays the groundwork for future research in utilizing quantum systems for time series analysis and prediction, offering a potential pathway to overcome limitations of conventional approaches.

We propose a novel approach where the reservoir is replaced by a quantum system, specifically a collection of coupled qubits, governed by quantum interference. The introduction of entanglement within the reservoir is hypothesized to significantly improve its ability to model and predict time series data. Theoretical analysis and simplified models demonstrate a potential for enhanced performance compared to classical reservoir computing methods. The core claim is that entangled quantum reservoirs can achieve superior time series prediction accuracy. This work lays the groundwork for future research in utilizing quantum systems for time series analysis and prediction, offering a potential pathway to overcome limitations of conventional approaches.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Quantum State Preparation
abstract: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental and often rate-limiting step in many quantum information processing tasks, including quantum computation, quantum communication, and quantum metrology. Traditional methods for preparing complex quantum states rely on iterative techniques, which can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to directly generate complex quantum states from classical inputs. The core idea is to train a GAN to learn the probability distribution of quantum states, effectively learning a mapping between classical data and corresponding quantum states. We formulate the problem as a minimax game between a generator and a discriminator, where the generator aims to produce realistic quantum states, and the discriminator aims to distinguish between generated and real quantum states. The mathematical formulation of this process is detailed below. We hypothesize that this approach will offer significant speedups compared to traditional state preparation methods, particularly for complex states. The success of this approach hinges on the ability of the GAN to accurately capture the intricate correlations inherent in quantum state distributions. This work provides a foundational framework for exploring the application of GANs in quantum state preparation and lays the groundwork for future research in this area.

title: Non-linear Quantum State Design for Adaptive Quantum Circuit Engineering
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum circuit design leveraging non-linear quantum states. Traditional quantum circuit design relies on pre-defined gate sequences and static parameter adjustments. This work introduces a self-adaptive circuit design method that dynamically adjusts the circuit's structure and parameters based on the inherent dynamics of the quantum state. We propose a machine learning-driven system to optimize the circuit's performance by continuously refining the circuit's configuration. The core mechanism centers around the quantification of quantum state evolution and its subsequent application to circuit design. The design offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, providing a more flexible and potentially high-performing solution for complex quantum circuit architectures.

title: Neuro-Graph Adaptive Optimization (NGAO)
abstract: This paper introduces Neuro-Graph Adaptive Optimization (NGAO), a novel approach to neural network optimization that leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) and reinforcement learning (RL) to achieve adaptive learning and generalization. The core claim of NGAO is that by dynamically adjusting the connection strengths and topology of a neural network, it can better adapt to evolving input data distributions, leading to improved efficiency and performance. NGAO operates by first using a GNN to analyze the current input data distribution represented as a graph, identifying optimization targets such as connection strength adjustments or node additions/deletions. Subsequently, a reinforcement learning agent, employing a policy gradient method, dynamically adjusts the network's connections and topology to maximize a reward signal, typically related to prediction accuracy or energy consumption. This iterative optimization process results in a neural network graph structure that more accurately reflects the current data distribution, ultimately enhancing performance. NGAO's key innovation lies in treating the neural network as a graph and utilizing GNNs and RL in a synergistic manner to enable adaptive optimization, particularly for non-static, dynamic data distributions, and proactive topological changes.

title: Dynamical System Representation of Neural Network Dynamics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to understanding and manipulating neural network dynamics by framing them as complex dynamical systems. We argue that neural networks, despite their complex architecture and training processes, exhibit behaviors that can be rigorously analyzed using the established tools of chaos theory and dynamical systems analysis. Specifically, we map the activation dynamics of a neural network onto a state-space representation, utilizing techniques such as Lyapunov exponents, bifurcation analysis, and Poincaré sections to characterize the system's behavior. The core contribution lies in demonstrating that the inherent complexities within neural networks – often considered solely as a result of training – can be attributed to underlying dynamical structures, potentially exhibiting chaotic behavior. This shift in perspective offers new avenues for enhancing network robustness, designing controlled transitions, and ultimately, achieving more predictable and reliable network performance. This work provides a theoretical framework for understanding and potentially controlling neural network dynamics, moving beyond traditional black-box training methodologies. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamic Geometry Transformation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers unparalleled opportunities for novel computation and information processing. This paper explores the dynamic geometry transformation of quantum entanglement, proposing a novel algorithm that generates entangled states with tailored distributions and leverages their geometric properties to enhance computational efficiency. We investigate the potential of this approach for applications in image processing and machine learning. The core mechanism centers around adapting the entanglement's geometric structure through a series of algorithmic operations, resulting in a system capable of generating complex and precisely controlled quantum states. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of entanglement's potential and highlights the advantages of a dynamically-oriented approach to quantum computation.

title: Probabilistic Resonance Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Probabilistic Resonance Networks (PRNs), a novel deep learning architecture designed to improve training speed and feature extraction capabilities by incorporating a probabilistic resonance mechanism. The core idea is to induce constructive interference among activations within a neural network layer, amplifying specific patterns. This is achieved through a layer with a tunable resonant frequency and phase shift, where activations are weighted based on their similarity to a reference vector. The PRN architecture offers a dedicated mechanism to generate resonance, potentially leading to faster convergence and improved performance compared to standard deep neural networks. We outline the theoretical framework, detail the PRN layer design, and discuss the potential benefits and future research directions.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Sensor Data
abstract: This paper explores the application of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) for real-time anomaly detection in sensor data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on static thresholds or rule-based systems, which are ineffective when dealing with complex, time-varying systems. DBNs offer a powerful alternative by explicitly modeling the temporal dependencies within the sensor data and learning the underlying system dynamics. The proposed approach constructs a DBN that represents the relationships between sensor readings and system states, continuously updating its model based on incoming data. Anomalies are identified as deviations from the learned model, enabling proactive detection and response. The core claim is that DBNs can accurately detect anomalies in real-time sensor data by learning the underlying system dynamics and identifying deviations from expected behavior. This research presents a novel methodology for real-time anomaly detection, providing a robust and adaptable solution for systems with dynamic behavior.

title: AIBuildAI-2.5: Efficient Autonomous AI Model Development Through LLM-Guided Tree Search
abstract: Autonomous agents that automatically build artificial intelligence (AI) models could broaden access to AI across science and engineering. A popular line of such agents frames model building as a code search problem and solves it by tree search, in which each node is a candidate program and the tree grows by generating a child program from a parent, and these agents now approach the capability of experienced AI engineers on realistic benchmarks. However, these agents have three weaknesses in efficiency that have not been fully addressed. First, only a small number of candidates can be executed within a realistic budget, so search rules that rank nodes by executed rewards, such as Monte Carlo-style tree search, rely on few and noisy scores and select the next node to explore less effectively. Second, no resource-aware strategy is used to schedule training jobs, which can lower hardware utilization and training efficiency. Third, every agent call is served by a single powerful model, which inflates inference cost. Here we introduce AIBuildAI-2.5, an agentic system that carries out the tree search with LLM agents and addresses each of the three issues. AIBuildAI-2.5 proposes a novel LLM-guided tree search, in which a judge scores each candidate on its expected improvement, grounding, and feasibility, and a selector ranks the pool of candidates from these scores and the state of the search. In addition, AIBuildAI-2.5 comprises a scheduler that launches training jobs with the current hardware resource status taken into account and a router that assigns lower-cost LLMs to less demanding tasks while reserving the most capable LLM for the most challenging sub-tasks in the AI model building workflow. AIBuildAI-2.5 ranks first on MLE-Bench with a medal rate of 73.3%, and outperforms a strong baseline on six autonomous AI research tasks from AIRS-Bench.

title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
abstract: Shared key--value (KV) cache reuse improves large language model (LLM) serving, but it can also create a timing side channel that reveals whether a prefix is already cached. Previous work shows that such attacks are possible, but their reliability under realistic multi-tenant contention is less understood. We study this problem through seven experiments on live shared LLM-serving systems. On a vLLM server running DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B on NVIDIA GB10, mean Cohen's d drops from 0.7789 with no synthetic workers to 0.2109 with two workers (t=8.412), while higher worker counts cause no statistically detectable further loss. A 120-run sparse-overlap experiment places the best breakpoint at the boundary of the measured range (tau=0, 95% CI [0.000,0.113]), supporting an ambient-versus-loaded regime change rather than an internal physical threshold. AUROC falls from 0.650 at ambient to 0.531 near 61% overlap and partially recovers to 0.574 at saturation. Concurrency-depth variance is the strongest measured correlate of effect size (r=-0.416) and hit consistency (r=-0.637). An interleaved control preserves the same non-monotonic ordering. The main collapse is also reproduced on a real two-node, two-GPU tensor-parallel vLLM setup, where mean d falls from 3.418 to 0.511 (p<0.01). Two SGLang pilots are statistically inconclusive. Overall, KV-cache timing reliability depends strongly on the load regime and serving stack, and measurements on quiet systems can overestimate operational attack reliability.

title: TransLearn: Representing and Comparing Transformer Architectures in a Free Categorical Framework
abstract: We define TransLearn, a free category of residual sequential architecture terms generated by a typed primitive signature. Its base doctrine is Cartesian with specified commutative-monoid operations on residual objects, rather than biproducts, so nonlinear Euclidean layers remain admissible. For a fixed signature, finite-graph completeness identifies the terms with finite acyclic typed architecture graphs modulo the stated Cartesian, monoid, and sequence-coherence equations; pure signature extensions are conservative on old terms. The syntax separates parameter identity, runtime routing, causality, state, and implementation labels. Finite depth-sharing patterns form the partition lattice; nested routed families flatten to a single routed family when dispatch and combine morphisms are unrestricted; and support certificates give a sufficient prefix-causality test for length-changing residual branches. Applied to Funnel-Transformer's published stride-2 mean pooling and repetition upsampling, the test leads to an explicit counterexample showing that their direct composition is noncausal if reused unchanged inside an autoregressive residual branch. The theory decides these structural questions; it does not decide optimization, accuracy, or hardware efficiency without additional interpretations or cost assumptions.

title: Lean 4 Confirmation and Approval Proof for Hamzah Equation. (51)
abstract:

Python import datetime import logging from typing import Any, Dict, List, Union import numpy as np # راه‌اندازی سیستم ثبت لاگ استاندارد صنعتی logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='[%(asctime)s] [HAMZAH-SOCIAL-ENERGY] : %(message)s') class HamzahSocialEnergyKernel: """ HamzahXcell: Social Energy & Entropy Collapse Kernel (Omega Production Grade) Calculates social energy, models inequality-driven entropy collapse via Hamzah's socio-quantum formula in 1155D. """ MANIFOLD_DIM: int = 1155 OMEGA_H_SQ: float = 1.38e20 # ثابتِ squared EPSILON: float = 1.155e-20 def __init__(self, cluster_id: str = "Hamzah_Social_Energy_Cluster") -> None: self.cluster_id: str = cluster_id self.timestamp: str = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") self.integrity_score: float = 1.0 logging.info(f"Initializing Social Energy Kernel for Cluster: {self.cluster_id} in {self.MANIFOLD_DIM}D.") def calculate_social_energy(self, info_flux: float, entropy_noise: float) -> Union[float, str]: """فرمولِ حمزه برای محاسبه انرژی اجتماعی و پایداری سیستم‌های انسانی بر اساس جریان اطلاعات و نویز آنتروپی""" if entropy_noise < 0.0: self.integrity_score -= 0.15 logging.error("خطای انرژی اجتماعی: نویز آنتروپی نمی‌تواند منفی باشد.") return "ERROR: Entropy noise cannot be negative." try: energy = (info_flux / (entropy_noise + self.EPSILON)) * self.OMEGA_H_SQ return float(energy) except ZeroDivisionError: self.integrity_score -= 0.2 logging.error("خطای بحرانی: تقسیم بر صفر در محاسبه انرژی اجتماعی.") return "ERROR: Division by zero encountered in social energy calculation." def run_collapse_simulation(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: """شبیه‌سازی فروپاشی اجتماعی: هرچه آنتروپی (نابرابری) بیشتر، پایداری و انرژی اجتماعی کمتر""" entropy_levels = np.linspace(0.1, 100.0, 100) # title: ViNoise-CSE: Contrastive Learning with Tone-Dropping Augmentation for Robust Vietnamese Text Classification
abstract: Vietnamese is a highly tonal language where the presence or absence of diacritics significantly alters word meanings. On social media, users often omit diacritics—either for typing convenience or to evade content moderation filters—which degrades the performance of standard NLP models. In this paper, we propose ViNoise-CSE, a contrastive learning framework that integrates a novel ToneDropper data augmentation strategy. By jointly training with tone-dropped positive pairs, ViNoise-CSE learns sentence representations that are resilient to diacritic omission. We evaluate our method on two downstream tasks: Hate Speech Detection (ViHSD) and Sentiment Analysis (VSFC). Experimental results show that the pure tone-dropping configuration of ViNoise-CSE significantly outperforms the strong PhoBERT baseline under extreme synthetic diacritic-loss conditions (+12.28% Macro-F1 at 100% tone dropping). Furthermore, the learned representations demonstrate exceptional stability, maintaining nearly flat performance across all noise levels (dropping only 1.49% F1 from 0% to 100% noise). Our semi-supervised variant (SupCon) substantially improves few-shot performance, yielding a +20.88% Macro-F1 gain over the baseline with only 1% labeled data. Finally, we provide a critical empirical evaluation showing that while contrastive pre-training excels in few-shot settings, simple supervised data augmentation outperforms it when full labeled datasets are available.

title: Dynamic Geometric Transformation Constraint
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometric transformation constraint algorithm based on quantum entanglement. Traditional constraint techniques often rely on static, individually-controlled constraints, limiting flexibility and potentially introducing instability. This work proposes a dynamically adjusted constraint system leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve a more robust and adaptable geometric transformation process. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to automatically fine-tune constraints, leading to significantly improved stability and controllability during geometric transformations. The core mechanism involves establishing entangled states to represent the transformation's state, allowing for a more nuanced and responsive adjustment of constraints.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Entanglement Propagation for Computational Geometry
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique pathway for manipulating information and creating complex correlations. This paper explores the algorithmic application of entanglement to propagate geometric information, aiming to facilitate the creation of intricate geometric structures and rigorous proofs of geometric theorems. The core mechanism centers around designing a "quantum map" – a state that utilizes entanglement to traverse geometric spaces, potentially enabling the generation of infinitely complex geometries. We present a novel algorithm that demonstrates the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its potential to revolutionize computational geometry and offer significant advancements in geometric analysis.

title: The Adaptive Quantum Topology Optimization Algorithm (AQO)
abstract: Quantum topology optimization (QTO) presents a novel approach to designing quantum circuits and algorithms with enhanced performance and efficiency. This paper introduces the Adaptive Quantum Topology Optimization Algorithm (AQO), a dynamically adjusting algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to automatically optimize quantum system parameters. The core mechanism centers around iterative adjustments to the quantum state, guided by a feedback loop that prevents the convergence to local optima. This research addresses limitations of current QTO methods by enabling automated exploration and optimization of complex quantum topologies. title: Teaching a Moving Student: Rethinking the Curriculum of On-Policy Distillation
abstract: In on-policy distillation (OPD), the student determines which states receive teacher supervision. As its policy evolves, earlier response prefixes become less likely even though teacher-student disagreement on them persists. Under matched trajectory and optimization budgets, neither more queries nor more frequent rollout resampling is uniformly beneficial. Current-policy rollouts outperform initial-policy rollouts at shorter response budgets, but this ranking reverses at longer budgets. Replaying initial-policy rollouts after current-policy training improves accuracy, whereas replaying fixed recent rollouts does not reproduce the gain. We propose R-OPD, a gradient-triggered curriculum that adaptively selects when to revisit initial-student trajectories. When changes in mean gradients fall within minibatch-level variation for two consecutive comparisons, training switches from the next iteration onward to initial-policy replay. Across eight mathematics benchmarks and three training-data orders, R-OPD improves average accuracy over continued current-policy sampling by 2.25/4.44 percentage points at 16K/32K for a 0.6B student and 2.81/6.15 points for a 1.7B student. With a 30B-A3B teacher, it improves 8B accuracy by 4.05 points at 32K. At 32K, R-OPD exceeds a fixed schedule of 40 current-policy updates followed by 20 replay updates by 1.39/1.66/1.85 points for 0.6B/1.7B/8B. At the same generation cap, R-OPD also produces longer responses, suggesting that well-timed revisits help students use more of their reasoning capacity.

title: Spectral bounds for the partial transpose
abstract: Among the various entanglement measures, the negativity stands out not only for its clear physical meaning but also for being directly computable from the spectrum of the partial transpose. However, the negativity captures only the total weight of the negative eigenvalues, whereas the finer structure of the negative spectrum remains largely unexplored. In this work, we fill this gap by introducing a hierarchical generalization of the negativity, the Ky Fan $k$-negativity, and developing a unified analytical framework for deriving spectral bounds on the partial transpose. To obtain the absolute bounds, we reduce the maximization problem to a spectral graph optimization, whose solution yields the exact bound for every $k$ through a single cubic equation. We further investigate these spectral bounds both analytically and numerically under a fixed-purity constraint. In particular, we solve the $k=1$ case completely and uncover a simple underlying graph structure. As two direct applications, we show that the Ky Fan $k$-negativity robustly certifies genuine multilevel entanglement and that it converts the $p_3$-PPT condition into a quantitative lower bound on the negativity.

title: Self-Organized Mapping for Complex Systems Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of Self-Organized Mapping (SOM) as a powerful technique for modeling and analyzing complex systems. Complex systems, characterized by emergent behavior, non-linearity, and interdependence, often present significant challenges to traditional modeling approaches. SOM, a type of neural network, offers a unique capability to discover underlying patterns and structures within these systems by projecting high-dimensional data onto a lower-dimensional grid while preserving topological relationships. This work presents a framework for utilizing SOMs to represent complex systems, detailing the process from data preparation and SOM initialization to model interpretation and validation. The core claim is that SOMs can effectively capture the intrinsic dynamics of complex systems. The core mechanism involves mapping system data onto a lower-dimensional space through the SOM algorithm's self-organizing process, resulting in a model that represents the system's state effectively. The novelty of this approach lies in its ability to identify and visualize complex relationships within systems that are often obscured by traditional analytical methods. The study focuses on the theoretical foundations and methodological considerations for applying SOMs to complex system modeling, without requiring experimental data.

title: Contextualized Attention Mechanisms with Recursive State Spaces
abstract: This paper introduces a novel attention mechanism that integrates recursive state spaces to address the limitations of conventional attention models in capturing long-range dependencies within sequential data. Current attention mechanisms, particularly those employed in deep learning architectures like Transformers, often struggle with effectively modeling relationships between distant elements in a sequence. This limitation stems from the inherent difficulty in propagating information across numerous time steps without explicit mechanisms for maintaining and updating contextual understanding. Our proposed approach utilizes a recursive state space to continuously accumulate and refine contextual information as the sequence is processed. This allows the model to generate more informed and contextually relevant attention weights, significantly improving its ability to model complex dependencies. We formulate the core mechanism as a system where the state space evolves iteratively, incorporating new information while retaining a memory of past observations. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual modeling, the potential of this approach to outperform standard attention mechanisms in scenarios demanding robust long-range dependency modeling. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the state space, allowing the model to selectively focus on relevant parts of the sequence based on a continually updated contextual representation. This work lays the groundwork for future research in attention mechanisms that are better suited for complex sequential data tasks.

title: Adaptive Control Flow Genetic Algorithm for Complex System Optimization
abstract: This paper presents the Adaptive Control Flow Genetic Algorithm (ACFGA), a novel approach to optimizing complex control systems. The ACFGA leverages the principles of genetic algorithms and control flow mechanisms to achieve adaptive control, effectively mimicking the process of biological evolution. The core idea is to represent control system parameters as genes within a genetic algorithm, employing selection, crossover, and mutation operators to drive the evolutionary process. Crucially, the algorithm incorporates an environmental feedback mechanism to assess the fitness of solutions and dynamically adjust parameters based on the changing environment. This allows the system to adapt and optimize itself over time. The proposed method offers a potentially powerful solution for tackling complex optimization problems where traditional methods struggle due to non-linearity, uncertainty, and dynamic environments. The theoretical framework and underlying mechanisms are detailed, showcasing the ACFGA's ability to evolve towards optimal control strategies. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated conceptually through the framework, highlighting its potential for real-world applications.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Exploration Bonuses
abstract: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) offers a promising approach to tackling complex sequential decision-making problems by decomposing them into simpler, manageable sub-tasks. However, a significant challenge in HRL lies in effectively balancing exploration and exploitation across the different levels of the hierarchy. Traditional HRL methods often rely on fixed exploration strategies, which can be suboptimal and hinder the discovery of optimal policies. This paper proposes a novel framework that addresses this limitation by introducing adaptive exploration bonuses at each level of the hierarchy. These bonuses dynamically adjust based on the uncertainty and complexity of the state space being explored, promoting more efficient and robust learning. The core idea is to provide each level with an incentive to explore regions of the state space that are either highly uncertain or particularly complex. This approach significantly improves the learning efficiency and robustness of HRL systems, particularly in environments with high dimensionality and intricate dynamics. The framework is presented with detailed mathematical formulations, outlining the key components and their interactions. We demonstrate, through a theoretical analysis, the advantages of this adaptive exploration bonus approach compared to conventional HRL methods.

title: Quantum Information Geometry Turing Domain
abstract: Quantum information geometry is a foundational concept in quantum information theory, offering a powerful framework for understanding and manipulating quantum states. This paper proposes a novel quantum information geometry Turing domain, characterized by its reliance on quantum entanglement and topological structures to define and analyze quantum information properties. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum information coding framework based on topological structures, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve robust and efficient information transfer and encoding. We argue that this approach significantly expands the scope of quantum information theory by extending the geometric interpretation of quantum states beyond traditional algorithmic applications.

title: Similarity of planning domain models via answer set programming
abstract: Automated planning is a prominent area of Artificial Intelligence, and an important component for intelligent autonomous agents. A critical aspect of domain-independent planning is the domain model, that encodes a formal representation of domain knowledge needed to reason about a given problem. Despite the crucial role of domain models in automated planning, there is a lack of tools supporting the knowledge engineering process by comparing different versions of the models, in particular, determining and highlighting differences the models have. In this paper, we formalise the notions of structural equivalence and strong equivalence of domain models, and, on top of these, we introduce a novel concept of similarity of domain models. To measure the similarity of two models, we introduce a directed graph representation of lifted domain models that allows the formulation of the domain model similarity problem as a variant of the graph edit distance problem. We propose an Answer Set Programming approach to optimally solve the domain model similarity problem, that identifies the minimum number of modifications the models need to become strongly equivalent, and we demonstrate the capabilities of the approach on a range of benchmark models.

title: FrontierMath Erdős
abstract: We introduce FrontierMath Erdős (FME), a benchmark of 68 Erdős problems that are open as of August 2026. To solve a task in FME, AI systems must resolve (prove or disprove) one of the 68 conjectures in the proof assistant Lean. Our 68 problems were selected by the second author among 652 open problems on erdosproblems.com for their mathematical interest and difficulty. AIs have recently resolved several open problems in mathematics, but these demonstrations fall short of a systematic study of AI capabilities. FME evaluates every AI model on the same fixed problems, autonomously and under the same budget. We evaluated five AIs with a budget of \$300 per problem. One (GPT-6 Astra) scored 3%, and all others scored 0%.

title: Quantum State Mapping: A Novel Approach to Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: Quantum state mapping is a rapidly evolving field with the potential to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. This paper proposes a novel algorithm, Quantum State Mapping, that leverages the inherent geometric properties of quantum states to directly guide the design of quantum circuits. By establishing a mapping between the underlying quantum state and circuit parameters, this approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional quantum algorithm design and unlock new possibilities for quantum device optimization. We introduce a mechanism centered around non-linear geometric transformations applied to quantum states to iteratively refine circuit parameters, leading to optimized circuit layouts with improved fidelity and reduced resource consumption. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments, showcasing potential for substantial efficiency gains in quantum circuit design.

Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on explicit computation, offering limited adaptability. This research leverages the inherent properties of non-linear graphs – specifically, their ability to represent and evolve data distributions – to automatically learn and model the data, facilitating more efficient computations and simulations. The algorithm incorporates a graph neural network (GNN) to provide a mechanism for model explanation and improve the algorithm's interpretability. The core claim is that this approach provides a significant advancement over existing quantum algorithms, offering greater flexibility, improved efficiency, and enhanced model explicability.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for secure communication and novel quantum technologies. This research investigates the application of quantum entanglement information entropy as a model for optimizing quantum state stability and developing a quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol. We propose a novel computational framework that leverages the unique properties of entangled states to quantify and manipulate entanglement, ultimately aiming to enhance the robustness and security of quantum systems. This study explores the potential of utilizing this approach to achieve improved qubit coherence and resilience against environmental noise. title: Temporal Relational Graph Learning with Causality Inference
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. However, many real-world graphs exhibit temporal dynamics, where relationships between nodes evolve over time. Furthermore, understanding causal relationships between nodes is crucial for predicting future states and generating robust representations. This paper proposes a novel Temporal Relational Graph Learning framework that integrates temporal convolution and causal Bayesian network inference within a GNN architecture. The core claim is that incorporating both temporal and causal relational information can significantly enhance GNN performance. We introduce a GNN architecture with a temporal convolution layer to capture evolving relationships and a causal Bayesian network inference module to estimate direct and indirect causal links. The resulting model learns embeddings that accurately model dynamic dependencies. We address the limitations of existing GNNs, which often lack robust methods for handling temporal dynamics and causal relationships, leading to unstable learning and inaccurate predictions. The proposed approach offers a pathway towards more sophisticated and reliable graph representations for time-varying and causally-informed applications.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Adaptive Structure Learning
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive structure learning algorithm for causal Bayesian networks designed to mitigate the limitations of existing methods. Current algorithms frequently exhibit sensitivity to noise and rely on stringent assumptions regarding causal relationships. This research addresses these challenges by integrating a Bayesian process model to quantify uncertainty associated with the causal structure. The proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the Bayesian network structure based on the process model's confidence estimates, effectively learning causal graphs from observational data. The core innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the learning process, allowing the network to evolve and refine its representation of causal dependencies as new information becomes available. The algorithm's robustness is significantly enhanced by explicitly modeling and incorporating uncertainty, resulting in a more reliable and accurate representation of causal relationships. The theoretical framework is presented, followed by a detailed description of the adaptive structure learning algorithm and its key components. Finally, we outline future research directions, including the incorporation of domain-specific prior knowledge and the evaluation of the algorithm's performance on a range of benchmark datasets.
